full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J.:- The instant Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 11.04.2011 complained of in the petition moved in Court today should not be set aside, and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The material facts relevant for disposal of the instant Rule as have been derived from the revisional application in short are that the opposite-party as plaintiff on 24.11.2009 instituted Title Suit being Title Suit No. 237 of 2009 in the 3rd Court of the Joint District Judge, Dhaka, alleging, inter alia, that the plaintiff is a monthly evictable tenant of the defendant. Thereafter, the defendant agreed to sale the schedule Flat as described in the plaint in favour to the plaintiff and fixed consideration money Tk. 20 lacs and out of the same the defendant took Tk.6 lacs and executed a Bainapatra dated 27.8.2005 in favour to the plaintiff but the defendant failed to execute the sale deed and hence the suit. 

3. In the Suit the plaintiff sought for the following reliefs:
“(ক) অত্র মোকদ্দমার নালিশী তফশিল বর্নিত ফ্লাটটি বাদী বিবাদীর নিকট হইতে বিগত ২৭-০৮-২০০৫ ইং তারিখের সম্পদিত বায়না চুক্তিপত্রমূলে বাদী মালিক ভোগ দখলকার মর্মে এক ঘোষনা মূলক ডিক্রি দিতে ফ্লাটের মালিক বিধায় তাহার বরাবরে ফ্লাটটি বিক্রয়/রেজিষ্টি দেওয়ার জন্য বাদীর পক্ষে ও বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে ঘোষনামূলক ডিক্রি দিতে।”

4. The defendant-petitioner entered appearance in the suit and submitted written statement denying the material, allegations made in the plaint and further stated that admittedly, the plaintiff is a monthly evictable tenant of the defendant since 1.12004 for the period of 2 (two) years and there was no agreement between the plaintiff and the defendant except the tenancy agreement. Further stated that the plaintiff ' has made Bainapatra for selling the suit Flat which is false and fabricated. It is further stated in written statement that the defendant instituted a suit against the plaintiff being Title Suit No. 225 of 2009 with a prayer that the defendant (plaintiff in the present suit) is a defaulter tenant and as such, evictable tenant under the plaintiff (defendant in the present suit) and prayer for eviction of the defendant from the suit property is the bona tide requirement of the plaintiff. The suit for eviction was decreed on contest against the contesting defendant vide judgment and decree dated 31 .1.2010 to the effect that; "The defendant is directed to hand over the possession of the suit property to the plaintiff within 90 days from this day in default the plaintiff will take his possession through Court. The defendant is hereby directed to pay due rent to the plaintiff within the date fixed". It has further stated by the defendant that the instant suit was filed with ill motive. Hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

5. While the suit was so pending the defendant as petitioner on 10.06.2010 filed an application under order 7, rule I1(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of 
the plaint of Title Suit No. 237 of 2009. The learned Joint District Judge after hearing both the parties by its judgment and order dated 11.04.2011 rejected the application for rejection of plaint under Order 7 Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

6. Being aggrieved by the impugned order dated 11.4.20 11 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3 Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 237 of 2009 the defendant as petitioner preferred the instant revisional application and obtained the instant Rule with an order of stay. 

7. Mr. S.N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the learned Joint District Judge committed an error of law in not considering the provisions of Section 17 (a) and 17(b) of the Registration Amendment Act, 2004 and as such, committed an error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order resulting in an erroneous decision occasioning failure of Justice. He has further submitted that the learned Joint District Judge committed an error in not considering the facts that the plaintiffs having had admitted in paragraph No.2 of the plaint that:
“অত্র মোকদ্দমান তফশীল বর্নিত ফ্লটটি বাদী ভাড়াটিয়া হিসেবে বসবাসের জন্য ০১-০১-০৪ ইং তারিখ হইতে ৩১-১২-০৫ ইং পযর্ন্ত ২(দুই) বছর মেয়াদিতে মাসিক ভাড়া ১২০০০/-(বার হাজার) টাকা ধায্য ক্রমে ২৪০০০/- (চব্বিশ হাজার) টাকা বাদীকে জামানত হিসাবে প্রদান করিয়া লিখিত চুক্তিপত্রের মাধ্যমে ভাড়া নিয়াছেন।”
 
The learned Judge did not address the above mentioned legal aspect of the case and as such, he has committed an error of law resulting erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice and as such, the same is liable to be set aside. He has further added that the settle principle of law as enunciated in the case of Most. Nurunnessa Vs. Mohibuddin Chowdhury reported in 5 BLT (HC)-36 wherein their lordships held that : 

“The Court can reject plaint only when it comes to the conclusion that even if all the allegations made in the plaint are proved still then the plaintiffs would not be entitled to any relief whatsoever,"

 In that view of the matter the learned , Judge ought to have allowed 'the application but committed an error in rejecting an application under order 7, Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

8. Mr. S.N. Goswami, the learned Advocate further submitted that the learned Judge committed an error of law in not considering the facts that the relationship between the plaintiffs and defendant is of landlord and tenant and it is admitted in paragraph No.2 of the plaint. Moreover, the defendant obtained decree against the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 225 of 2009 for evicting the - plaintiff from the suit property. The plaintiff without taking legal steps against the judgment and decree of eviction with ill motive filed the instant suit only for dragging the decree of eviction which has been obtained by the defendant as mentioned and as such, the Court below committed an error of law in rejecting the application for rejection of the plaint. 

9. Mr. Goswami in support of his contentions referred to the case of Abdul Jalil and others Vs- Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd, reported in 9 BLT,(AD)- 71 and to the case of Mahar Ali Matbar Vs. Daliluddin Chowkider reported in 31 DLR (HCD)- 392. He further relied to the case of Sremati Niotio Rani and others -versus-Azit Kumar and others reported 21 BLT (HCD)- 155. He also relied on to the case of Md. Banazir Ahmed Vs. Dahendra Chandra Saha reported in 4 BLT (AD). 

10. No one appears to oppose the Rule. 

11. We have considered the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and also perused the referred precedents. On perusal of the plaint which is annexure 'A' to the revisional application it appears that the plaintiff in paragraph No.2 admitted that he was a tenant from 1.1.2002-31.12.2005 under the defendant. He further admitted in paragraph No.4 that defendant being needed cash money he proposed to sell the property and further consultation amongst the party the plaintiff was agreed to purchase the property on consideration of TK. 20,00000/- and out of which he paid TK. 1,00000/- on 21.08.2005. It has been asserted by the plaintiff that on 25.8.2005 the defendant has received TK.5,00,000/- through pay order and thereafter they made an agreement on non judicial stamp on 27.8.2005. Considering above noted facts it appears that the plaintiffs in his plaint himself submit in 2(two) characters one is tenant and another as purchaser, however, on going through the whole plaint we find nothing that as tenant he has surrendered his tenancy ship before entering in the agreement for sale. 

12. Now the question before us whether a tenant without terminating his tenancy ship can made a contract to purchase the suit property. On perusal of annexure B(2) it appears that before filing the instant suit for declaration of title by the plaintiff opposite-party the present petitioner as plaintiff filed title suit No. 225 of 2009 against the opposite party plaintiff for eviction the opposite party from the premises as tenant. In that suit the petitioner got the decree of eviction however, the plaintiff opposite party without taking any legal steps against that judgment and decree of eviction he filed the instant suit for declaration of title. It further appears from the annexure -B that the petitioner on 20.3.2006 served notice under section 106 of the transfer of property Act to the plaintiff opposite party terminating the relationship of land lord and tenant between the plaintiff and the defendant. It appears that while the period of notice has already been expired the defendant petitioner was compelled to file an eviction suit being Title Suit No. 301 of 2007 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 1st Court Dhaka. The plaintiff also in paragraph No. 12 admitted that the defendant petitioner filed the aforesaid Title Suit in the Court of Assistant Judge, I" Court, Dhaka for eviction the plaintiff from same suit property. Eventually, said suit was transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, 10th Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 225 of 2009 which was decreed. 

13. From this fact it is apparent on the face of the record that the plaintiff filed the instant suit praying the reliefs which has been mentioned elsewhere in the judgment. On perusing a prayer it seems to us that the reliefs sought in the present suit not in accordance with Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. For convenience of discussion and clarification of this legal issue we feel, it would be noteworthy to quote the Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act which are as follows: Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. 

"42.Discretion of Court as to declaration of status or right -Any person entitled to any legal character, or to any right as to any property, may institute a suit against any person denying, or interested to deny, his title to such character or right, and the Court may in its discretion make therein a declaration that he is so entitled, and the plaintiff need not in such suit as for any further relief:
Bar to such declaration- Provided that no Court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff, being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration of title, omits to do so. Explanation- A trustee of property is a "person interested to deny" a title adverse to the title of someone who is not in existence, and for whom, if in existence, he would be a trustee." 
14. We have gone through the referred decision placed before us by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. On perusal of 1 the case of Abdul Jalil and others Vs. Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd. it appears that our Apex Court has held that where a plaint cannot he rejected under order 7, rule I I of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court may in its inherent jurisdiction can reject the plaint taking recourse of Section 151 Code of Civil Procedure. 

It further held to the referred case of Most Nurunnessa Vs. Mohibuddin Chowdhury. 

"The Court can reject the plaint only when it comes to the conclusion that even if all the 'allegations made in the plaint are proved still then the plaintiffs would not be entitled to any relief whatsoever"
It further appears that it has been held to the case of Mahar All Matbar Vs. Daliluddin Chowkider reported in 31 DLR (H.C.D.)- 392. 

"Mere execution and registration of a sale deed ipso facto does not pass title to the purchaser. Intention is consideration paramount and it can be inferred from circumstances." 

"Intention of the parties is the paramount consideration in determining whether title will pass to the purchaser on execution and registering ipso facto will not pass title to the purchaser" 

"Gathering of intention is a function of the Court of fact. When the kabala indicates otherwise the onus lies heavily on the plaintiff to prove that the real intention was otherwise. Intention is a state of mind and it has to be gathered from circumstances" 

15. On discussing the above precedents it seems to us that if we consider the plaint and pray& of the ease we find nothing in the provisions of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act that reliefs sought in the plaint can lie given. Because mere facts that by dint of unregistered bainapatra dated 27.09.2005 the plaintiff neither accrued any right and title over the suit property. The plaintiff did not file the suit for Specific Performance of Contract, rather, for declaration of title in the year 2009 whereas before that some provisions of the Specific Relief Act, Registration Act and Transfer of Property Act have already amended in the year 2004 by giving effect from the 15 July, 2005 by which clearly , barred to file the suit for Specific Performance contract by unregister Bainapatra. Thus, it was incumbent upon the plaintiff if he made any contract for purchase on 27.8.2005 that must be registered otherwise that contract would be nugatory as it is against the provisions of law of the section 21 of the Specific Relief Act. Furthermore as per section I7A and 17B of the Registration Act the parties made any unregistered contract for purchase of any land in violation with provisions of that sections that would be void and ambition. More-so in deciding present case it would not be to refer section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act wherein define the sale as per section 54 sale is transfer of ownership not exchange for price paid or price part paid part promised on. 

16. So, according to the defendant on sale deed of agreement for sale must be admitted facts and for which the plaintiff can seek relief as per section 12 of the Specific Relief Act. However, the pleadings and circumstances as has been stated in the plaint we find nothing that a contract for sale if so-facto would be a documents passing title and decide against the defendant if that agreement is not admitted. Rather the defendant petitioner file a suit for eviction of the plaintiff of the instant suit and in that case the petitioner obtained a decree against the plaintiff for eviction from the suit property and while the decree is effective and alive the plaintiff by filing a suit later cannot get any declaration for title as prayed in the plaint in the present case. It is our considered view that when it has been established that the plaintiff opposite-party is tenant under the defendant petitioner and a competent Court has passed a decree for eviction against the plaintiff and that decree is in operation and is still in enforceable in such a situation the plaintiff cannot prayed for declaration of title in regard the same property unless earlier decree is set aside and as such, no decree can be passed. Therefore, we are of the view that if we take view that the assertion made in the said pleadings as a whole is correct, even then, the plaintiff would not be entitled to get any relief as prayed for. 

17. Thus, from the facts and Circumstances of the present case and the discussions made hereinabove and considering precedents referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioners we find substance in the Rule. 


18. Thus, the Rule having merit, it succeeds. 

19. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order passed on 11.04.201 1 is set aside. 

20. The application for rejection of plaint is allowed. Accordingly, the plaint of Title Suit No. 237 of 2009 is hereby rejected, 

21. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated. 

22. The office is directed to communicate the judgment and order to the concerned Court below. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. A. B. M. Khairul Haque ------ For the petitioners
Mr. S. A. M. Mahabub Elahi with Mr. Md. Emdadul Haque Azad ------ For opposite-party No. 1
parties:
General Manager, Sonali Bank & Ors. ------ Petitioners.
Versus
Md. Abul Khaiyar & Ors. ------ Opp. parties.
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Mozammel Hoque, J:- This Rule was issued directing the opposite-party No. 1 to show cause as to why the order dated 12.11.89 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Kishoreganj, in Other Suit No. 289 of 1986, should not be set aside. 

	2. The opposite-party No. 1 Md: Abul Khayer being plaintiff instituted the afore-said suit, namely, other suit No. 289 of 1986 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge challenging the order of termination of service vide No. MYM PO/PF (GA1/2379 dated 24.11.1986 being void, illegal, inoperative, ultravires and has no binding effect upon him and also for a declaration that the plaintiffs service as Driver of Sonali Bank was still continuing with all salaries and benefits. In the Aforesaid suit the defendant No 4 and 6 appeared and filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for rejecting the plaint on the ground that no advalorem court fee was paid and that the forum for challenging such an order of termination of service was the Labour Court and not the ordinary Civil Court. After hearing both the parties and perusing the materials on record, the learned Subordinate Judge, by his order dated 12.11.89, rejected the application of the defendant Nos. 4 and 6 filed under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, finding that the advalorem court fee is not necessary, in a suit like this and that since the order of termination was challenged in the suit, it is not barred under any law before the Civil Court.

	3. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 12.11.89 the defendant-petitioners preferred this Revisional application and obtained the present rule. 

	4. Mr. A. B. M. Khairul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that admittedly the plaintiff was a Driver of Sonali Bank and in the eye of law he is a worker. If he has got any grievance about the service matter, he is required to file an application in Labour Court and not in the ordinary Civil Court. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred to the case of Managing Director Rupali Bank Vs. Tafazzal Hossain, 44 DLR (A.D.) 260. In the aforesaid judgment their lordships of the Appellate Division held as follows:-
	"In the instant case, this principle shall apply. Respondent, admittedly a worker, filed this suit, challenging the legality of his termination from service, before the Civil Court whose jurisdiction to entertain the suit stood ousted by necessary implication. That he, when the Labour Court was there his remedy law before that Court only. Ouster of a court's jurisdiction many be provided by express words as also by necessary implication. In this case the appellate Court hold the suit maintainable relying upon the Single Bench decision in the 39 DLR, 167-case, but this decision is palpably erroneous. The decision by the other Single Bench in the 41 DLR, 94 case is found to be perfectly correct." 
	In the above decision their lord-ships held that:-
	"The Labour Court is the only forum for a worker/workman to seek remedy against grievance relating to his employment. In the instant case of Respondent, who felt aggrieved by his termination, remedy lay before the Labour Court under Section 25(1) of the Standing Orders Act". Their lordships further held in that judgment that jurisdiction of a Court goes to the very root of a matter. If the Court gets no jurisdiction, everything shall fall through. Their lordships also held that if any legal remedy is ordinary available under both general law and special law, the remedy prescribed by the special law must be sought in exclusion of the general law. 

	5. Relying upon the aforesaid decision the learned Advocate submits that since the jurisdiction of the Civil Court is barred and the remedy of a worker is, in fact, lies in the Labour Court under the special law, a Civil Court has no jurisdiction to entertain such a suit. In the aforesaid case their lordships considered two Single Bench decisions, one reported in 39 DLR and another reported in 41 DLR. The distinguishing feature between the present case and the case reported in 41 DLR is that there the office bearers of the trade union were aggrieved persons which is not in the present case inasmuch as in the present case the worker of the Bank, who is not an office bearer, is the aggrieved person. Mr. Mahabub Elahi, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 has drawn our attention to the proviso to section 25(b) of the Standing Orders Act as stood on the day of termination of service in 1981 and sub-mitted that since there was a legal and specific bar to challenge the order of termination before the Labour Court by a worker under the proviso to section 25(b) of the Standing Orders Act, the present plaintiff-opposite-party No. 1 had no other alternative but to file the present suit in the Civil Court. Unamended proviso to section 25(b) of the Standing Orders Act as stood on the day of termination of service runs as follows:-
	"Provided that no complaint shall lie against an order of termination of employment of a worker under Section 19 unless the worker concerned is an officer of a registered trade union and his employment is alleged to have been terminated for his trade union activities or unless the worker concerned, whether an officer of a registered trade union or not, has been deprived of the benefits specified in that section." 
	He has also referred to the amended provision of the proviso to Section 25(b) of the said Act which came into force by an amendment in 1985. Amended proviso to Section 25(b) runs as follows:-
	'Provided that no complaint shall lie against an order of termination of employment of a worker under Section 19, unless the service of the worker concerned is alleged to have been terminated for his trade union activities or unless the worker concerned has been deprived of the benefits specified in that section." 

	6. In the instant case the impugned order is the order of termination of service of the worker concerned, Mr. Elahi submits that the Labour Court was totally debarred from entertaining such a com-plaint from the worker against termination service dated 24.9.81 and if the Labour Court entertained any such com-plaint, it would have been absolutely with-out jurisdiction. So, the worker had no other alternative but to challenge the order of termination in the Civil Court. Relying also upon the above decision reported in 44 DLR (A.D) Mr. Elahi submits that in the instant case, had the Labour Court entertained an application from the plaintiff against his termination order, it would have acted beyond its jurisdiction as per provisions of proviso to Section 25(b) of the Standing Orders Act inasmuch as in the present case un-amended proviso to Section 25(b) of the Act would have been applicable. 

	7. It appears to us that in course of bearing of the aforesaid case of 44 DLR (A.D) the learned members from the party failed to bring the barring clause contained un-amended proviso to Section 25(b) of the Act to the notice of their lord-ships and argue on the said proviso to Section 25(b) in juxtaposition with the provisions of section 19 and 25(a) of the Act. According to un-amended proviso the plaintiff at the relevant time was neither an officer of the trade union nor his service was terminated for any trade union activities nor he prayed for any benefit under Section 19 of the Act from which he was deprived. In the above reported case leave was granted mainly to consider that as to whether the Administrative Tribunal got jurisdiction to try the case of the plaintiff and alternatively it was argued that if the Administrative had no jurisdiction, then the Labour Court was the actual forum inasmuch as the plaintiff was a worker/workman, and as such Civil Court had no jurisdiction to entertain a suit against an order of termination of service of a worker. We are fully aware that the decisions of the Appellate Division are binding upon this Court constitutionally. But with due respect we like to mention that we find, some distinguishing feature in the present case from the case reported in 44 DLR (A.D.) as stated above, in as much as un-amended proviso to Section 25 (b) of the Act was not directly brought before their Lordships for consideration. 

	8. In this connection we may refer to the case of Bangladesh Small Industries Corporation vs. Mahbub Hossain Chowdhury 29 DLR (S.C), 41. In that case an employee of the BSIC challenged the order of termination of his service from the Corporation which was a statutory body and in enunciating the principle of challenging the order of termination their lord-ships held as follows:-
	"A review of all these decisions, as have been referred to above shows that preponderance of judicial authorities have helped the formulation of certain well reasoned principles as to the law relating to the employees of a statutory Corporation as administered by the Superior Courts in their writ jurisdiction as well as by the ordinary civil Courts. We are concerned in these two appeals with the statutory bodies of public character, viz. Bangladesh Small Industries Corporation and Janata Bank and the law governing the employees of such bodies may be-- briefly stated as follows :-(a) If an employee is dismissed or his service is terminated in contravention of a mandatory statutory provision, the employee has a right of action either in a Superior court in its Writ jurisdiction or in a Civil Court. (b) If the service of its employee is terminated in violation of the principle of natural justice, the employee has a., similar right of action as in (a). (c) If the office is a statutory one, the holder of the office has similar right of action as in (a) in termination of the said office not in accordance with the law, under which the said office has been created. So, the principle laid down in this decision is that if the service of an employee is terminated illegally, the Civil Court has got the jurisdiction to entertain a suit challenging such termination. In the case of Karnaphuli Paper Mills Sramik Union vs. Registered Trade Union, 42 DLR 329 It is held that if there is no remedy for the grievance of the plaintiff in the Industrial Relations Ordinance, then the civil Court will have jurisdiction to try the matter. Mr. Mahabub Elahi submits that in the Standing Orders Act specific bar was put upon the Labour Court from entertaining any application wherein termination of the service of a worker is challenged. The said Act has not provided any other forum to ventilate the grievance of a worker if he is legally aggrieved by an order of termination of service. 

	9. In the instant case it clearly appears that the opposite-party No. 1 being plain-tiff instituted the suit challenging the termination of his service. Since no forum to challenge the termination of service had been provided in the Standing Orders Act or in the Industrial Relations Ordinance on in any other rule and regulation of the Bank concerned, we are of the view that the Civil Court had got the jurisdiction to entertain such a suit challenging the order of termination inasmuch as the plaintiff being worker had no other forum to challenge this order of termination from ser-vice. From the plaint it appears that termination of service was not challenged on the ground of any trade union activities of the plaintiff worker; rather it is alleged in the plaint that one Abdus Sattar, a temporary go down keeper of the Bank, was the nephew of the Regional Manager of the Bank, Mr. Mobarak Ali That Abdus Sattar had got personal enmity with the plaintiff when they both lived in a mess, and this termination of service of the plaintiff was the result of high handed action of the Regional Manager Mr. Mobarak Ali. 

	10. Whether the termination was legal or not is not the question before us. The point raised there is that when the Civil Court had got jurisdiction to entertain such a suit the relevant time inasmuch as the worker had got the alternative statutory forum to ventilate his grievance in the Labour Court. After considering the materials on record as well as the decisions cited above by the learned Advocate, we are of the view that the Civil Court had got the jurisdiction to entertain such a suit wherein the termination of a worker had been challenged there inasmuch as the un-amended proviso to Section 25(b) of the Standing Orders Act as quoted above had put a clean embargo upon Labour Court to entertain an application challenging the order of termination of service of a worker. 

	11. We have perused the impugned order and found that the learned Subordinate Judge in deciding this matter has not committed any error of law occasioning any failure of justice and as such there is no reason to interfere with the impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. 

	12. In the result, this Rule is discharged without any order as to costs and let the suit be proceeded with in the Trial Court in accordance with law. Since it is an old case, the Trial Court is directed to hear and dispose of the suit within six months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment.

	End.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Afzal Hossain, Advocate ----- for the petitioners 
Mr. S. Rashed Jahangir, D.A.G with Mr. Titus Hillol Rema A.A.G ----- for the Respondent No.1
parties:
Sarwar Alum Chowdhury being dead his legal heirs: 1(ka) Fazilatun Nessa Mimi and others -----   Petitioners
Versus
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works & others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. J. N. Deb Choudhury, J: On an application under article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh made by the petitioners, this Court on 04.05.2002 was pleased to issue a Rule Nisi in the following terms: 

"Let a Rule Nisi issue calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the 
impugned judgment and order dated 31.07.2000 passed by the respondent No. 2 as contained in Annexure 1 to the writ petition should not be declared without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why the disputed Plot No. 13/A/A/1st Colony Mirpur, Dhaka should not be released from the "ka" list of the abandoned building as published in the Bangladesh Gazette Extra Ordinary on 23.09.1986 and pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

2. Relevant facts necessary for disposal of this Rule, in brief, is that, the predecessor-in-interest of the vendor of the petitioners, Syed Abdus Sattar was allotted a house at the Mirpur Coloney, popularly known as Mirpur 1st  Coloney vide agreement dated 24.07.1953 (Annexure-A to the writ petition). Thereafter, Syed Abdus Sattar while was in peaceful possession of the said property died on 25.03.1971 leaving behind his only nephew Md. Ehsanul Hoque as his heir and since then Md. Ehsanul Hoque was in peaceful possession of the property in question without any hindrance from any quarter. Thereafter, the petitioner's vendor Md. Ehsanul Hoque sworn an affidavit before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka on 19.05.1979 to the effect that he is the only surviving heir of late Syed Abdus Sattar, the original allottee under the Muslim Personal Law and he also obtained a succession -certificate on 14.04.1979 in Succession Certificate Case No.241 of 1979 from the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for the purpose of recovering loan money left by Syed Abdus Sattar from one Mr. Md. Nazrul Islam amounting to Tk. 925.00 (Annexure-B1 to the writ petition). The writ petitioners also stated that on 25.05.1979 they purchased the said property being House No. 13/A/A, Mirpur 1st  Coloney tinder police Station Mirpur, Dhaka by two registered sale deeds from Md. Ehsanul Hoque and since the date of purchase the petitioners are paying all rent, taxes, bill etc. to the Revenue Office, WASA, DESA and City Corporation and their names were duly recorded in the Government Revenue Office and in the recent land survey conducted by the Government and thereby possessing the said property peacefully; but, the Government most illegally enlisted the property in question in the abandon property 'Ka' list, published in the official Gazette at page 976 (ka). It has further been stated that on 22.11.1983 the section officer of the Ministry of Public Works served a notice upon the petitioners for showing the original deeds and also served similar notice on 08.04.1984. While the writ petitioners submitted his documents and was advised to file an application before the Court of Settlement and accordingly, the petitioners filed case No. 125/96 (Ka-4, first Coloney, (Mirpur), Dhaka and the same was ultimately heard and dismissed on 31.07.2000, with the findings that the writ petitioners failed to prove the facts that his vendor was the heir of the original allottee and also found that the property was rightly enlisted as abandoned property.
 3. Being aggrieved with the judgment and order of the Court of Settlement, the petitioners filed the writ petition and obtained the Rule Nisi. 

4. Respondent No. I contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition and supported the judgment and order dated 31.07.2000 passed by the learned Judge of the 1st Court of Settlement, the respondent No. 2 on stating that the writ petitioners annexed some forged and manufactured papers in order to establish his alleged false ownership and the Government has legally and rightly enlisted the property as abandoned property and also staled that the writ petitioners failed to show the whereabouts of the original allottee, Syed Abdus Sattar after 28.02.1972. 

5. During pendency of the Rule the petitioner Nos. I and 2 died and their heirs were duly substituted. 

6. Mr. Md. Afzal Hossain, the learned advocate for the petitioners takes us through the Writ Petition as well as the annexure thereto, the materials on record and submits that the original allottee Syed Abdus Sattar died on 25.03.1971 leaving behind his only nephew Md. Ehsanul Hoque as his only heir and accordingly, the said Md. Ehsanul Hoque while in possession of the property in question sworn an affidavit before the Magistrate, 10 Class, Dhaka on 19.05.1979 declaring that he was the sole heir of Syed Abdus Sattar (Annexure-B to the writ petition) and also referred the succession certificate dated 14.04.1979 (Annexure-B1 to the writ petition) showing that Md. Ehsanul Hoque obtained the succession certificate from the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for the purpose of recovering - a loan of Tk. 925.00 as heir of the original allottee Syed Abdus Sattar and while Md. Ehsanul Hoque was in possession sold the land in question to the writ petitioners by two registered sale deeds dated 25.05.1979; but, the Government most illegally enlisted the property in question in the abandon property 'Ka' list, published in the official Gazette at page 976 (ka). He also submits that the inclusion of the disputed property in the 'ka' list has been without any lawful authority as the petitioners were in possession, till illegally dispossessed by the lessees of the Government. He also submits that after purchase the writ petitioners paid taxes to the Dhaka Municipality Corporation and the bills of gas connection. He further submits that the Government by Memo dated 08.04.1984 (Annexure-F to the writ petition) admitted the vendor of original writ petitioner as owner of the land in question; but, the Court of Settlement without considering those documents most illegally dismissed the case by the impugned judgment and order dated 31.07.2000, which is liable to be set-aside and the disputed Plot No.13/A/A, 1st Coloney, Mirpur, Dhaka is liable to be released from the `ka' list of the abandoned building as published in the Bangladesh Gazettee Extra Ordinary, on 23.09.1986. Mr. Hossain further submits that, in view of petitioners possession in the disputed property the same cannot be enlisted in "ka" schedule of the abandoned property. The learned advocate for the petitioners by citing two decisions reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55 and 54 DLR (AD) 100 and submits that notice as contemplated under sections 5 & 7 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (hereinafter referred as the Ordinance) was not issued upon the petitioner and as such the inclusion of the disputed property in the list of abandoned property is without lawful authority. Mr. Hossain, the learned advocate also referred a decision reported in 45 DLR 416 and submits, it is a condition precedent that the physical possession of a building must have to be taken over by the Government before enlisting any property in 'ka' list of the abandoned property. On referring those decision and facts as stated above the learned advocate for the petitioners prays for making the Rule absolute. 

7. On the other hand, Mr. S. Rushed Jahangir, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondent No. I takes as through the affidavit-in-opposition and annexure thereto and submits that the petitioners failed to prove before the Court of Settlement that the original allottee or his legal heirs if any, were present in Bangladesh on or after 28.02.1972 and also submits that the writ petitioners in order to grab the land in question created some false and forged documents and the Court of Settlement rightly disbelieve the documents filed by the writ petitioners. The learned .Deputy Attorney General also placed before us the relevant article 2(1) and 6 of the President Order 16 of 1972 and section 5(2) of the Ordinance and also cited some decisions reported in 48 DLR (AD) 10, 3 BLC (AD) 42, 61 DLR (AD) 15, 49 DLR (AD) 161 and 59 DLR (AD) 165 and submits that in view of these decisions of our Apex Court, Govenment has no obligation to prove the property as abandoned property and it is only the writ petitioners who have to prove that the property is not abandoned property and also submits that, it is immaterial whether the abandoned property listed in 'Ka' or 'KW list of the abandoned property list as published and as such, he prays for discharging the Rule. 
8. We have heard the learned advocate for the petitioners as well as the learned Deputy Attorney General for the respondent No. I and perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and annexure thereto. 

9. It appears from the order sheet of this Court that by order dated 20.01.2009 this Court directed the respondent No. 2 to transmit the case record of Case No. 125 of 1996 (ka-4) regarding the House No. 13/A/A of 1‘1 Coloney, Mirpur, Dhaka and accordingly, the record has been transmitted to this Court. 

10. We have carefully examined the record of the Court of Settlement, and found that the writ petitioners examined 2(two) witnesses in order to prove their case before the Court of Settlement, amongst them P.W. I is Mohammad Nazrul Islam. who is a witness of the sale deeds dated 25.05.1979 and P.W. 2 Mohammad Siraj-Ud- Dowla also a witness of the sale deeds dated 25.05.1979 and they were examined only in order to prove the execution of the registered sale deeds dated 25.05.1979 and also filed the affidavit dated I 9.05.1979 and the succession certificate dated 14.04.1979 in order to prove that Md. Ehsanul Hoque was the only heir of Syed Abdus Sattar the original allottee along with some other papers. 

11. The petitioners though stated in the writ petition that the original allottee had died on 25.03.1971 leaving behind his only nephew (sister's son) Md. Ehsanul Hoque as his heir and. in order to prove the said fact filed two documents, one is an affidavit which was sworn before the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka on 19.05.1979 (annexure-B to the writ petition) and the other is a succession certificate dated 14.04.1979 (annexure-B1 to the writ petition). From those documents it appears that Md. Ehsanul Hoque on 19.05.1979 sworn an affidavit before the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka declaring himself as the sole heir of Syed Abdus Sattar and it appears from the succession certificate dated 14.04.1979, the same was obtained for recovering a loan of Tk. 925.00 only, while said Md. Ehsanul Hoque transferred the case land in question by two registered sale deeds dated 25.05.1979. So, it appears to sly that only for the purpose of creating sale deeds dated 25.05.1979. showing Md. Ehsanul Hoque as the heir of Syed Abdus Sonar, the succession certificate dated 14.04.1979 and affidavit dated 19.05.1979 were obtained. Moreover, the writ petitioners failed to produce any documentary or oral evidences before the Court of Settlement to prove the fact that the original owner Syed Abdus Satter or his legal heir was present in Bangladesh and occupied managed or supervised the disputed property when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into operation. 

12. Now let us consider the decisions placed before us by the respective parties. The learned advocate for the petitioners relied upon the case of Bangladesh Vs Amela Khanmn and others, reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55. wherein our Hon'ble Appellate Division held that, 

"High Court Division further found that according to clause (6) of sub-section (1) of .section 5 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance 1985 an abandoned property in possession of a person can only be included in. the "kha" list of abandoned buildings in respect of which notice for surrendering or taking possession has been issued. Though the learned Deputy Attorney General referred to notices dated  06.11.1976, 07.06.1977 and 06.03.1986 mentioned in the judgment of the Court of Settlement he could not satisfy us that the said notices were issued to surrender possession of the disputed property treating the same as abandoned property. On going through the judgment of the Court of Settlement we find that those notices were issued on the respondent Now /-6 to produce their vendor Bibi Homaira when they had applied far mutating their names oiler their purchase from Bibi Homaira. Thus it appears that the Government petitioner did neither treat the disputed property as abandoned property nor took any step to take over possession of the some till publication of Gazette notification in question. Since no notice as contemplated under section 5(1)(h) of the said Ordinance was issued to the respondent Nos. 1-6 or any other person inclusion of the disputed property in the "kha" list of the abandoned buildings is without lawful authority. In that view of the matter we do not find any merit in this petition to interfere with the impugned judgment." 
And in the case of Government of Bangladesh and others Vs. Bibi Minium and other, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 100 wherein their Lordships held that, 

"It is now settled principle of law on interpretation of section 5(1)(b) of the Abandoned Buildings (supplementary provision) Ordinance, 1985 in the case of Bangladesh vs Amela Khatun and other 53 DLR (AD) 55 that since no notice as contemplated under section 5(1)b)of the Ordinance was issued to the respondent or any other person inclusion of disputed property in the kha' list of the abandoned building is without lawful authority. In the Pets and circumstances of the case as detailed above and Plea by the High Court Division and that the judgment of the Court of Settlement is coram non judice, the illegal inclusion of the building in the 'kha' list of the abandoned building and that no notice having been served to the petitioner or other predecessor, the said inclusion is without any lawful authority." 

And in the case of lqbal Ahmed Quraishi Vs. Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Works, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Dhaka, reported in 45 DLR 416,. wherein a Division Bench of the High Court Division held that, 

"Therefore, it is a condition precedent that the physical possession of building most have been taken over by the Government before it could be listed as an abandoned property under Clause (a) of sub-section (I) of section 5 of the Ordinance i.e. published in the official Gazette."

 On the other hand, it appears from the decisions cited by the learned Deputy Attorney General in the case of Government  of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Mil and others, reported in 48 DLR (AD)10, that their Lordships held that, 

"The Government has no obligation either to deny the facts alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property merely because the same is disputed by the claimant." And in the case of Hazerullah and another Vs. Chairman, 1st Court of settlement and another, reported in 3 BLC (AD) 42, their Lordships held that, "This contention will stand only when the claimant can prove that the disputed building was not an abandoned property. In case before the Court of settlement, main question is, whether the disputed house answers the description of "abandoned property" as defined in article 2 (I) of Bangladesh Abandoned property (C'ontrol, inanagemnt4 and Disposal) Order, 1972(P0 No. 16 of 1972), briefly, 

"the Order". Under clause (1) of Article 2 of the Order 'abandoned Property, inter alts, means any property owned by any person who is not present in Bangladesh or whose whereabouts are not known or who has ceased to occupy, supervise or manage in person his property. Section 5(2) of the Ordinance provides that a list of the buildings published under suchsection ( I ) thereof shall be conclusive evidence that the buildings included therein are abandoned property and have vested in the Government as such. 

Before the Court of Settlement the petitioner could nor product any evidence that the said Abdur Robins or his alleged heirs had been present in Bangladesh during alter the war of liberation and that their whereabouts were known to the respondent Government or that the said Abdur Rahim had been occupying supervising and managing the disputed property as on 28-2-72. The said court on consideration of the materials on record held that the original lessee Abdur Rahim and his heirs at the relevant time were not traceable in Bangladesh and that the appellants had unauthorized been occupying the property in question since 28-03-72. As such, it is immaterial as Jar as the appellants are concerned whether the disputed property was published in the `Ka' or 'KW list." 
(Bold, emphasis given) 

And in the case of Golam Rabbani Vs. Chairman, Court of Settlement and others, reported in 61 DLR (AD) 15, their Lordships decided as under: 

"In the case of Hazerullah vs Chairman. 1st Court of Settlement reported in 3 BLC (AD) 42 it was held that it is immaterial whether the disputed property was listed in the 'ka' or 'Ma' list, it is the abandoned character of the property which is the main criteria for determining the whole matter." And in the case of Government of Bangladesh Vs. Ashraf Ali @ Ashraf Ali and another, reported in 49 DLR (AD) 161, wherein their Lordships held that, 
"It has been held by this Division in various decisions that the enlistment of a building under section 5(1) of the Ordinance 54 of 1985 raises a presumption in law that the property is an abandoned property under section 5(2) of the Ordinance. This presumption is, of course, a rebuttable presumption but respondent No. I failed to rebut this presumption. No rebuttable evidence could be adduced to show that original owner Yahiya was present in Bangladesh and he occupied, managed or supervised the disputed building when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into operation. Hence, the listing of the property as an abandoned property in the Supplementary Provisions Ordinance, 1985 was lawful as it was an 'abandoned property by operation of law." 

And lastly in the case of Rowshan Am Begum Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Works and Urban Development, Government of Bangladesh and others, reported in 59 DLR (AD) 165. wherein their Lordships held that, 

"In the instant case the petitioner having not been able to establish before the Court of Settlement that the claimant of the property or for that matter her vendor Anwari Khatun were present in Bangladesh on 28.02./972 and consequent thereupon the property having had assumed the character of abandoned property, the listing of the property in question. even if without service of notice as per provision of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985, is not material an the property because of non service of notice for listing in the list of abandoned properties would not cease to be an abandoned property and consequent there upon the claim of title made by the petitioner in the property in question in not legally sustainable" 

13. On considering the facts and circumstances of the case we are of the view that the writ petitioners failed to prove that Syed Abdus Sattar or his legal heir ever occupied, managed or supervised in person the land in question on or after 28.02.1972. Only 2(two) witnesses were examined by the writ petitioners before the Court of Settlement to prove the execution of the alleged sale deeds of 1979 and no other oral or documentary evidences were produced before the Court of Settlement to prove the petitioner's case. Moreover, the enlistment of the disputed property under the Ordinance raises a presumption in law that the property is an abandoned property tinder section 5(2) of the Ordinance. This presumption is, of course, a rebuttable presumption but the petitioners failed to rebut this presumption. No rebuttable evidence could be adduced to show that original owner Syed Abdus Sattar or his legal heir was present in Bangladesh and had occupied, managed or supervised the disputed building when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into operation. Hence the listing of the property as an abandoned property was lawful as it was an abandoned property by operation of law. Further, the  petitioners having not been able to establish before the Court of Settlement that their vendor Syed Abdus Sattar was present in Bangladesh on or after 28.02.1972 and consequent thereupon the property having assumed the character of abandoned property, the listing of the property in question, even if without service of notice as per provision of Ordinance, is not material as the property because due to non-service of notice for listing the property in the list of abandoned property would not change the fact that the property is an abandoned property and consequent, there upon the claim of title made by the petitioners in the property in question is not legally 
sustainable. The Government has no obligation either to deny the facts alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property merely because the same is disputed by the petitioners. It is immaterial whether the disputed property was listed in the 'Ica' or 'kha' list, it is the abandoned character of the property which is the main criteria for determining the whole matter. 

14. We as such, find that the writ petitioners failed to prove their case that their vendor 
Md. Ehsanul Roque was the heir of the original allottee Syed Abdus Sattar and that Syed Abdus Sattar or his legal heir had occupied, managed or supervised the property in question on or after 28.02.1972 and the same was rightly listed as abandoned property. Therefore, the Court of 
Settlement rightly found that,
 	“প্রার্থী পক্ষের দাখিলী কাগজাদি এবং সরকার পক্ষের দাখিলী সরকারী নথি পর্যালোচনা্ করিলাম। নালিশী সম্পত্তি সরকার জনৈক মোহজের (Refugee) আবদুস সাত্তারের অনুকূলে কিছু শর্ত সম্বলিত অরেজিট্রিকৃত লিজ্ব এশ্রিমেন্ট মূলে বিগত ২৪-৭-৫৩ ইং তারিখে বরাদ্দ প্রদান করেন, ইহা সর্বস্বীকৃতা প্রার্থীগনের দাবী হইল লীজ গ্রহীতা আবদুস সাত্তার নিঃসন্তান অবস্হায় বেক্রোর ছেলেকে একমাত্র  য়ারিশ রাখিয়া মারা গলে এহসানুল হক লীজ গ্রহীতার উত্তরাধিকার সূত্রে মালিক হিসাবে নালিশী সম্পত্তি বিগত ২৫-২-৭৯ ইং তারিখে প্রার্থীগনেৱ অনুকূলে বিক্রয় করে এবং খরিদা সূত্রে থ্রার্থীগন বর্তমাংন  বিক্রয় করে এবং খরিদা সূত্রে  থ্রার্থীগন বর্তমাংন নান্দিশী সম্পত্তি… ভোগ দখল করিতেছে। সরকার পক্ষ প্রার্থী পক্ষের এই দাবী অস্বীকার করিয়া উল্লেখ করেন যে, লীজ গ্রহীতা স্বাধীনতা যুদ্ধের সময়ে স্বপরিবারে এদেশ ত্যাগ করে এবং স্বাধীনতার পর হইতে এ যারত তাহার অবস্হান অজ্ঞাত নিঃসম্ভান্ম অবন্হড়ায় এদেশে তাহার মৃত্যু এবং এহসানুল হক তাহার ণ্…বানের ছেলে ইহা প্রার্থীপহ্মের কাল্পনিক গল্পই বটে৷ তৎমর্মে কোন প্রকার স্বীকৃত কাগজাদি প্রার্থী পক্ষ দাখিল করে নাই৷ প্রার্থী পক্ষের দাখিল করে নাই৷ প্রার্থী পক্ষের ১ নং সাক্ষী জনাব নুরুল ইসলাম ত্তেরােভে বলেন তিনি প্রাথীগনের খরিদা দলিলে স্বাক্ষী আছেন। বিস্তু এই সাক্ষী দলিলে কিলিখা আছে বা কত টাকা লেনদেন হইয়াংছ তৎমর্মে কিছুই বলিতে পারেন না ৷ এই স্বাক্ষী ১৯৭৬ সাল হইতে ১৯৭৯ ইং সাল পর্যন্ত এই বাড়িতে এহসানুল হকের ভড়ােটিয়া ফ্লি বলিলেও এহসানুল হক কিসূষেন বাড়ির মালিক ফ্লি কিছুই বলিতে পারেন না  এই সাক্ষী আরও স্বীকার করেন যে, ১৯৭৬ সালের  পূর্বে নালিশী সম্পত্তি পরিত্যক্ত অবস্হায় জ্জি ৷ ২ নং স্বাক্ষী ত্তনােব সিরাজউদ্দৌলা জেরাতে এহসানুল_ হক কিভাবে নালিশী সম্পত্তির মালিক হইয়াছেন সেই সম্পর্কে কিছুই বলিতে পারেন নাই ৷ এই ক্ষেত্রে নালিশী সম্পত্তির লীজ গ্রহীতার একমাত্র ওয়ড়ারিশ সূত্রে এহসানুল হক নালিশী সম্পত্তির মালিক বা দখলকার ছিলেন ইহা প্রমান করিতে পারেন নাই৷ মূল মালিকের মৃত্যু ও তাহার ওয়ারিশ সম্পর্কে স্বীকৃত প্রমান প্রার্থীপক্ষ যেহেতু দাখিল করিতে ব্যর্থ হইয়াছেন সেইহেতু প্রার্থীপক্ষ তাহাদের মোকদ্দমার প্রার্থীত প্রতিকার পাইতে পারেন না। সেইহেতু তাহাদের মোকদ্দমা খারিজযোগ্য
 
15. Accordingly, we do not find substance in the arguments of the learned advocate for the petitioners and find substance in the arguments of the learned Deputy Attorney General for the respondent No.1.

16. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

17. Send down the record of the Court of Settlement.

18. Communicate the judgment to respondent No. 1at once.
End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal. J:- This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 18.02.1999 (decree signed on 25.02.1999) passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Nilphamari in Money Suit No.1 of 1998 decreeing the suit.

2. Material facts of the case as necessary for the disposal of the appeal are that the Deputy Director of Family Planning, Nilphamari (in-charge) as plaintiff filed a suit being Money Suit No. 1of 1998 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Nilphamari impleading the present appellant, G. M. Abu Hena and 6(six) others for realisation of money amounting to Tk.2,26,435.64 on the averments that wife of the defendant No.1, Most. Monowara Begum was in service as Family Planning Inspector till 31.8.1987 under the revenue budget, who thereafter joined in the higher post under the development project as Senior Family Planning Inspector on 01.9.1987 and during service died on 30.7.1989 and as such she is not entitled to get any pension benefit; that after the death of said Monowara Begum her husband defendant No.1, G. M. Abu Hena in connivance with other defendants withdrawn pension and other benefits of deceased Monowara Begum amounting to. Tk. 2,26,435.64; that the plaintiff is entitled to recover the said amount from the defendant No.1 inasmuch as Monowara Begum (now deceased) in order to get promotion took retirement from the post of Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget and joined to the higher post under the development project as Senior Family Planning Inspector on 01.9.1987. Hence the suit.

3. The defendant No.1 (present appellant) contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner inasmuch as the plaintiff in his personal capacity filed the suit for realization of the Government money without obtaining any power to file the suit. It is further contended that his wife deceased Monowara Begum never tendered her resignation from the post of Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget in order to join in the higher post under the development project. The defendant's case is that there is nothing wrong on the part of the defendant No.1 inasmuch as who after the death of his wife Monowara Begum applied for pension and other benefits to the Government in accordance with law and the concerned authority of the Government on examining the same allowed him to withdraw pension and other benefits as legal successor of the deceased Monowara Begum and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

4. At the trial the plaintiff himself was examined as PW-1 and only contesting defendant himself was examined as DW- 1 to prove their respective cases.

5. The learned subordinate Judge on consideration of the materials on record decreed the suit holding that the defendant No. 1 most illegally withdrawn the pension benefit of her deceased wife Monowara Begum and as such he is compelled to deposit the said pension benefit amounting to Tk.2,26,435.64 in the treasury of the Government within one month.

6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 18.02.1999 (decree signed on 25.02.1999) the present defendant No.1 as appellant preferred the instant First Appeal before this Court.

7. Mr. Md. Rasheduzzaman Basunia, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-appellant submits that the impugned judgment and decree is not based on correct evaluation of the facts and materials of the case nor on proper appreciation of the evidence on record and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. He next upon placing the circular/ notification of Ministry of Establishment under Rule 1 dated 28.11.1994 vide memo No. সং-সম/বিধি-১/এস-২/৯৪(অংশ-২)-২৪১(২০০), submits that the impugned judgment and decree is perverse being contrary to the Nitimala of the Government dated 28.11.1994 vide its memo No. সং-সম/বিধি-১/এস-২/৯৪(অংশ-২)-২৪১(২০০),

8. Mr. Basunia, the learned Advocate further in the course of his argument after placing the plaint of the suit, deposition of witnesses and other materials on record submits that as per Nitimala if an employee under revenue budget is joined to the higher post under development project leaving his former rank he/she will not get pension benefit but in this case the plaintiff miserably failed to prove that deceased-Monowara Begum leaving her former rank under revenue budget promoted to the higher post under the development project. He further points out that the claim of the suit is cryptic in nature inasmuch as it is apparent from the record that after the death of Monowara Begum, her husband defendant No. 1 approached to the concerned authority for pension benefit of his deceased wife and thereupon, the concerned authority of the Government after thorough scrutiny into the matter gave pension benefit of deceased Monowara Begum to the defendant No.1 as legal successor of Monowara Begum and in that view of the matter it does not lie in the mouth of the plaintiff or anybody else that on practicing fraud the defendant No. 1 managed to withdraw the pension benefit. Mr. Rasheduzzaman Basunia, finally upon referring to the decisions reported in 9 BLT(AD) 66 and 39 DLR(AD) 237 submits that the proposition of law is well settled that there may be thousands of defects in the documents of the defence as well as their case but that does not entitle, the plaintiff to get a decree. The burden lies on the plaintiff to prove his case and he must succeed on his own strength only and not at the weakness of the defendant and in this case the plaintiff miserably failed to prove that the wife of defendant No.1 in order to get higher post took her own retirement from the post of Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget and thereafter, she was promoted to the higher post as Senior Family Planning Inspector under the development project and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

9. On the other hand, Mr. Arobinda Kumar Roy, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the respondent No.1 supports the impugned judgment and decree which was according to him just, correct and proper. He submits it is apparent from the material evidence on record that deceased-Monowara Begum was all along in service under the revenue budget till 31.8.1987 and as such it is the duty of the defendant No.1 to prove that his wife did not take retirement from the post of Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget in order to get higher post as Senior Family Planning Inspector under the development project but in this case the defendant-appellant did not or could not produce any scrap of paper to show that Appellant's wife Monowara Begum never took her own retirement from the post of Assistant Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget. The learned Assistant Attorney General to fortify his contention has relied on the decision reported in 7 BLD 156.

10. We have heard the leaned Advocate for the appellant and the learned Assistant Attorney General for the respondent at length and perused the materials on record including the plaint of the suit, deposition of witnesses and the impugned judgment and decree.

11. To appreciate the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides from a correct angle, let us see first how far the learned Subordinate Judge was justified in passing the impugned judgment and decree. The definite case of the plaintiff-respondent being that wife of the appellant took retirement from the post of Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget and thereafter, joined to the higher post under the development project and as such she is not entitled to get any pension benefit.

12. At the trial the plaintiff, Dr. Reajul Islam himself was examined as PW-1, who in his deposition stated that wife of defendant No.1 joined in service on 11.01.1968 and she was in service under the revenue budget till 31.01.1987. This witness also stated that: তিনি ০১/৯/৮৭ ইং তারিখে পদোন্নতি পাইয়া উন্নয়নখাতে ঊর্ধতন পরিবার কল্যান পরিদর্শিকা হিসাবে চাকুরী করিতে থাকেন এবং ৩০/৭/৮৯ ইং তারিখ মারা যান ৷ তার ওয়ারিশরা বিধি বহির্ভূতভাবে পেনশন ও ভাতা যার পরিমান ২,২৬,৪৩৫/৬৪ টাকা উঠাইয়াছেন ৷ যাহা ১ নং বিবাদী অন্যান্য বিবাদীর সহযোগীতায় উঠাইয়াছে ৷ ১নং বিবাদীর স্ত্রী যেহেতু উন্নয়ন খাতের কর্মচারী তাই তিনি পেনশন ভাতা পাইতে হকদার নহেন ৷ This witness in his cross-examination stated that: আমি নিজ নামে ভুলে মামলা করিয়াছিলাম ৷ যাহা পরে সংশোধন করা হইয়াছে সরকার আমাকে মামলা করার অনুমতি দিয়াছেন। তাহার কাগজ দাখিল করিতে পারি I This witness in his cross-examination also stated that he could not say the nature and manner of collusion in between the defendant No. 1 and other defendants.

<u>13. On a careful perusal of the averments of the plaint together with the deposition of PW-1, it appears that the plaintiff-respondent in support of his case that the wife of the defendant appellant No.1 took retirement from the post of Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget for joining to the higher post under the development project could not produce any scrap of paper. It is also found from the evidence of PW-1 that he did not produce any document to show prior to filing the suit he obtained permission from the Government.</u>

14. Now, let us examine the circular dated 28.11.1994. The relevant portion of the circular dated 28.11.1994 vide its memo No. সং-সম/বিধি-১/এস-২/৯৪(অংশ-২)-২৪১(২০০) reads as follows:

বি���য়ঃ- রাজস্বখাতের পদধারীগনকে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের উচ্চতর পদে প্রেষনে নিয়োগ/নিয়োগ/পদোন্নতি প্রদান এবং রাজস্বখাতের স্বপদে প্রত্যাবর্তন সম্পর্কিত নীতিমালা ৷

(ক) প্রেষন ব্যাতীত রাজস্বখাতের কোন কর্মচারীকে প্রকল্পের কোন পদে  নিয়োগ/অস্থায়ী নিয়োগ/বদলী করা যাইবে না ৷ তবে রাজস্বখাতের কোন কর্মচারী স্বেচ্ছায় সরাসরি নিয়োগের সকল আনুষ্ঠানিকতা পালন পূর্বক উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে নিয়োগ লাভ করিলে তাহাকে রাজস্বখাতের পদ হইতে পদত্যাগ করিতে হইবে এবং এইক্ষেত্রে উক্ত কর্মচারী প্রকল্পের নব-কর্মচারী হিসাবে গন্য হইবেন ও তাহার পূর্বেকার রাজস্ব খাতের চাকুরীৱ কোন সুবিধা তিনি পাইবেন না ৷

(খ) রাজস্বখাতের কোন কর্মচারীকে কেবল স্বীয় পদমর্যাদা সম্পন্ন এবং  রাজস্বখাতের পদের মূল বেতন স্কেলের (টাইম স্কেল অন্তর্ভূক্ত নয়) সমষ্কেলের পদে প্রেষনে নিয়োগ দেওয়া যাইবে।........

From the above, it transpires that if any employee took retirement from his service under the revenue budget for joining to the higher post under the development project, he/she is not entitled to get pension benefit.

15. We have already indicated that in this case the plaintiff-respondent could not or did not produce any scrap of paper to show that the wife of defendant-appellant voluntarily tendered her resignation from the post of Family Planning. Inspector under the revenue budget for getting higher post under the development project. Defendant. No.1, G.M. Abu Hena, husband of the deceased- Monowara Begum, who in his evidence as well as written statement categorically stated that his wife Monowara Begum never took retirement from the post of Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget in order to get higher post under the development project. This witness in his deposition stated that: আমার স্ত্রী  মনোয়ারা রাজস্ব খাতে চাকুরী করিতেন। সে পদোন্নতি পাইবার পরও রাজস্ব খাতে ছিল। রাজস্ব খাত হইতে তার চাকুরী উন্নয়ন খাতে যায় নাইI  So, we find there is a good deal of substance in the contentions raised by Mr. Rasheduzzaman Basunia, the learned Advocate for the appellant that the plaintiff respondent by adducing sufficient evidence failed to prove that the wife of defendant No.1 took retirement from the post of Family Planning Inspector in order to join higher post under the development project.

16. In the case of Golzar Ali Pramanik Vs. Musammat Saburjan Bewa being dead her heirs Md. Yakub Ali Khan and others reported in 9 BLT(AD) 66, it has been held that:

"There may be thousands of defects in the documents of the defence as well as their case but that does not entitle, the plaintiff to get a decree. The plaintiff is to prove his case irrespective of the defence version of the case and from the materials on record it appears that the plaintiff failed to prove genuineness of their documents and also their possession. This aspect of the matter escaped the notice of the High Court Division in the aforesaid Second Appeal and in such circumstances the finding of the High Court Division is wrong and cannot be sustained."

Ongoing through the entire materials on record, it appears that there is nothing on record to suggest that the wife of defendant No.1 took retirement from the post of Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget in order to get higher post under the development project.

17. The proposition of law is well settled that the burden lies on the plaintiff to prove his case and he must succeed on his own strength only and not at the weakness of the defendant. Therefore, we are led to  hold that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and decree without applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstance of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice.

18. Mr. Arobinda Kumar Roy, the learned Assistant Attorney General at the end of the day having himself realized the fate of the case upon referring to a decision reported in,7 BLD(AD) 156 submits that law does not require that all facts alleged by the plaintiff shall be strictly proved, it is the duty of the defendant to prove his case and in this case the defendant by adducing sufficient evidence failed to prove that she did not join to the higher post under the development project after taking retirement from the post of Assistant Family Planning Inspector under the revenue budget.

19. To meet this last branch of argument of Mr. Arobinda Kumar Roy, the learned Assistant Attorney General, we have carefully studied the decision reported in 7 BLD(AD) 156 and it seems to us that the principle as enunciated in the cited decision in no way help the plaintiff-respondent in the facts and circumstances of the case rather it helps the defendant-appellant. Therefore, the contention raised for the aforesaid reasons are of no substance.

<u>20. Furthermore, on assessment of the entire materials on record we find nothing wrong on the part of the defendant-appellant inasmuch as who after death of his wife Monowara Begum as legal successor applied for pension benefit of her deceased wife and thereupon, the concerned authority of the Government after thorough scrutiny over the matter allowed the defendant appellant to withdraw the pension benefit of her deceased wife.</u>

21. In view of our discussions made in the foregoing paragraphs vis-a-vis the decisions reported in 9 BLT (AD) 66, 39 DLR (AD) 237 and 7 BLD(AD) 156 it is by now clear that the instant appeal must succeed.

22. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree dated 18.02.1999 (decree signed on 25.02.1999) passed by the Subordinate Judge,1st Court, Nilphamari in Money Suit No.1 of 1998 is set-aside.

23. Let a copy of this judgment along with lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.
