full_judgment:
Mr. J. N. Deb Choudhury. J:- The Role was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 03.08.2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Banskhali, Satkania Chowkhi, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 178 of 2002, should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs filed other Suit No. 178 of 2002. before the Court of Assistant Judge, Banskhali Sadar, Satkania, Chittagong 'for declaration that the registered deed of instrument dated 10.05.2001, appointing Mohontha to be illegal, collusive. without jurisdiction etc. and not binding upon the plaintiffs and for permanent injunction. 
3. The plaintiffs' case in brief, is that, the plaintiff No. 1 is nephew of Sreemat Swami Adhayatananda Puri Maharaj and both are devotees of Rishidham established by Sreemat Swami Adhayatananda Puri Maharaj. Sreemat Swami Adhayatananda Puri Maharaj bought 6.40 acres of land on 30.12.1950 from R.S. Khalian No. 79/8 and A.S. Plot No. 8 in Certificate Case No. 260/50-51 and constructed Rishidam "Ashram thereon and appointed Sree Sadananda Puri (Kamini Palit) as Mohanta/manager of the Ashram and he was acting as a Principal of the Ashram and applied, for lease in the name of Swamiji Sadananda Puri in Settlement Case No. 35/60-61; but, unfortunately he died on 2nd Baishak, 1373 B.S before settlement of the said land and was buried at Sree Sree Tulushidham. Before his death he was appointed as Mohanta of Sree Sree Tulushidham vide registered deed dated 24.03.1961 by the Mohanta Sree Joy Rafi Das. Sree Sadananda Puri made a transfer deed on 18.3.1967 in favour of Sreemat Swami Atchutananda Puri Maharaj who also paid rent. Sreemat Swami Adhayatananda Puri Maharaj was not entitled by deed of appointment of mohanta dated 24.03.1961 by Joyram Das to appoint next mohanta and Sreemat Swami Adhayatananda Puri Maharaj did not appoint anybody as mohanta. Joyram as vide registered trust deed dated 08.01,1970 handed over all power of Tuluaiihidham and conducted ceremony of mehantaship of Sreemat Swami Atchulananda Puri Maharaj. One Satya Ranjan Mohejan as alleged Secretary of Sree Guru Sangha instituted Other Suit No. 17 of 1978 before the Court of 2nd Judge, Chittagong which was dismissed on 23.03.1983. One Satya Ranjan Singh as chairman of Sree Guru Sangha filed Other Suit No. 89 of 1979 before the Court of 2nd Judge. Chittagong for declaration of title and confirmation of possession. The said suit on transfer renumbered as Other Suit No. 210 of 1984 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Patiya, Chittagong. Said Satya Ranjan Singh also instituted Other Suit No. 14 of 1985 before the Court of , Subordinate Judge, Patiya. Chittagong against the managing committee of Hrishidam and the said suit. was dismissed on 31.12.1987. Thereafter, on perusal of the daily Azadi dated the plaintiff - came to know that alleged chairman of the Sree Guru Sangha namely Prafulla Ranjan appointed as mohanta of Hrishi Dham and Tulusi Dham performing birthday ceremony of Sreemat Swami Adhayatnanda Puri Maharaj. The plaintiff on 01.06.2002 collected the certified copy of the registered appointment deed dated 10.05.2001, which was illegal and hence filed the suit. 

4. After filing of the suit the plaintiffs on 22.07.2002 (Annexure-B to the Civil Revision) filed an application for amendment of plaint for deleting the stated status of defendant No. I and insertion of a new address of the said defendant No. I and -for insertion of a schedule of lands to the plaint and for addition of "Upazilla Nirbahi Officer, Bangskhali, Chittagong" as a defendant in the suit. But subsequently by an application dated 25.07.2002, the plaintiffs prayed for deleting the prayer for addition of party of "Upazilla Nirbahi Officer, Bangskhali, Chittagong" 

5. The defendant No. I on 03.08.2002 (Annexure-C to the Civil Revision) filed a written objection against the application for amendment of the plaint and prayed for rejection of the application for amendment of plaint on stating that the defendant No.1 already appeared and also filed written objection against the application for temporary injunction and also contended that concurring the schedule of land as stated in the application for amendment of plaint, the plaintiffs did not pray any relief and as such, the application for amendment is liable to be rejected. 

6. By the impugned order dated 03.08.2002, the 'learned Assistant Judge, Banskhali. Chittagong, allowed the prayer for amendment of plaint against which the defendant No. I filed the, present Civil Revision and obtained the instant Rule. 

7. Mr. H.S. Deb Brahman. the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the plaintiffs in the cause title of the plaint admitted the status of defendant No. 1 as “শ্রীমৎ সুদর্শানান্দ পুরী ধর্মীয় গুরু পিতা শ্রীমৎ স্বামী অদ্বৈতানন্দ পুরী মহারাজ” which also admitted in other paragraphs of the plaint and such admission cannot deleted by way of amendment. He next submits that by the proposed amendment the plaintiffs for insertion of some lands against which plaintiffs did not pray any relief. In support of his submission he relied upon the decision in the case of Abdul Wadud Contractor and another Vs. Nazir Ahmed and others, reported in I MLR (AD) 233, wherein their Lordships held that, 
"the introduction of certain new, facts and subsequent cause of action different from those made in the plaint will change the nature and character of the suit"

 8. Mr. Deb Borman also relied upon a decision in the case of Akitullah and others Vs. Zafala Beguম and others, reported in 10 BLT (AD)132. wherein  their Lordships held that, 	"Before allowing any amendment to the plaint the Court mast come to a finding that such amendment is necessary fern determining the real question in controversy between the parties and that the same shall not change the nature and character of the suit." 

9. And accordingly, he prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

10. On the other hand, Mr. Subrata Saha, the learned advocate appearing for the plaintiffs-opposite party Nos. I and 2 contested the Rule by filing counter affidavit and submits that by the proposed amendment the plaintiffs only prayed for changing the address of the defendant No.1 and the schedule of land as stated in the application for amendment are the land of the registered instrument dated 10.05.2001 under challenge and the nature and character of the suit by the proposed amendment and further submits that the trial court on proper consideration of the plaint, application for amendment of plaint and other documents rightly allowed the application for amendment of plaint and accordingly, he prayed for discharging the Rule. 

11. In order to appreciate the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the parties, I have gone through the Revisional application, impugned order and other materials on record very carefully. 

12. Now, the question calls for consideration whether the learned Judge of the Trial Court below committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order. 

13. It appears that in the proposed amendment there are two parts, one relating to change of status and address of the defendant No. I of the suit and the second part for insertion of some lands in the plaint. It appears that while filed the suit the plaintiffs prayed for declaration of the registered instrument dated 10.05.2001 to be illegal, collusive and without jurisdiction; but, did not give any schedule of the land of that registered instrument dated 10.05.2001 in the plaint, though the plaintiffs filed an application for temporary injunction and according to the learned advocate for plaintiff-opposite parties, the same is still pending before the Trial Court. 
14. Be that as it may, by the first part of the application for amendment the plaintiffs admitted the status of the defendant No. I as “শ্রীমৎ সুদর্শানান্দ পুরী ধর্মীয় গুরু পিতা শ্রীমৎ স্বামী অদ্বৈতানন্দ পুরী মহারাজ” and the defendant No. l already appeared in the suit. The plaintiffs in the application for amendment also did not state any cause and reason for changing the status of the defendant No.1 

15. It is an establish principle of law any admission made in the pleading by any of the parties to the suit, gave a right to the other side and the admission as made by the respective parties regarding status specially in this case as made by the plaintiffs with the name of the defendant No. 1 as “শ্রীমৎ সুদর্শানান্দ পুরী ধর্মীয় গুরু পিতা শ্রীমৎ স্বামী অদ্বৈতানন্দ পুরী মহারাজ” cannot be allowed to omit or delete by way of amendment. 

16. In view of such facts so far the first part of the application for amendment concerning change of status of defendant No. 1 cannot be allowed as the admission of the plaintiff in the plaint given a right to the defendant No. 1 which cannot be taken away. 

17. So far the second part of the proposed amendment of the plaint concerning insertion of some land as schedule to the plaint, appears to be cogent and reasonable and such insertion do not change the nature and character of the suit and those are necessary for proper adjudication of the dispute in the suit. 

18. The decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner as reported in I MLR (AD) 233 and 10 BLT (AD) 133 are not relevant in the facts and circumstances of the present case in as much as the plaintiffs are not inserting any new facts or any subsequent cause of action or the second part of the proposed amendment did not change the nature and character of the suit. 

19. In a case of M/s. Modi Spinning &Weaving Mills Limited and another Vs. Ladha Ram & Company, reported in. AIR 1977 (SC) 680, it has been held by the' Indian Supreme Court that, it is true than inconsistent pleas can he made in pleadings but the effect of substitution of paragraphs 25 and 26 is not making inconsistent and alternative pleadings but it is seeking to displace the plaintiff completely from the admissions made by the defendants in the written statement if such amendments are allowed the plaintiff will be irretrievably prejudiced by being denied the opportunity of extracting the admission from the defendants. The High Court rightly rejected the application for amendment and agreed with the trial Court."

20. In view of the discussions and observations made above this Court is of the view that deleting or omitting the admission by way of amendment, cannot be allowed as in this case admission regarding status of the defendant No.1 as prayed for in the first part of the proposed amendment cannot be allowed by way of amendment: but, the second part of the proposed amendment inserting a schedule of land are liable to be allowed. 

21. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute in part by rejecting the first part of the proposed amendment regarding status and address of the defendant No. 1 and allow the second part of the proposed amendment regarding insertion of a schedule of lands in the alit as prayed by the plaintiffs vide application for amendment dated 22.07.2002. 

22. Since, the suit is of the year 2002 the Trial Court is hereby directed to dispose of the suit within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment. 

23. However, there will be no order as to costs. 

24. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. 

25. Communicate the order to the court below at-once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker J:- Leave was granted calling upon the opposite party Nov.1-4 to show as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 10.07.2011 passed by the 
learned District Judge, Thakurgaon in Civil Revision No.7 of 2010 affirming the judgment and order dated 09.03.2010 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Haripur, Thakurgaon in Title Suit No.70 of 2008 should not be set aside and / or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem lit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can he stated thus the present opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit No.82 of 2004 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Thakurgaon which was subsequently transferred to the Court of learned Assistant Judge. Haripur Thakurgaon and renumbered as Title Suit No.70 of 2008. The present petitioner as defendant No.10 contested the suit by filing written statement. When the suit was pending for hearing before the trial Court the present petitioner on the ground of his illness submitted adjournment prayer. Thereafter the suit was fixed on 09.03.2010 for further preemptory hearing which was cross-examination of the witnesses of the defendant Nos.I-2 and 5. The present defendant-petitioner on that date prayed time for further hearing on the ground of his sudden pain in chest supported by Medical certificate and the plaintiff made his appearance in the form of filing iliajira'. The defendants witnesses did not file 'hajira' and remain absent. The learned Assistant Judge rejected the defendant's prayer for time and fixed a date for hearing argument. 

3. Being aggrieved the defendant preferred a Civil Revision being No.7 of 2010 in the Court of learned District Judge, Thakurgaon and the learned District Judge hearing the parties disallowed the Civil Revision affirming the order of the trial Court by the impugned judgment and order dated 10.07.2011.

4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order the defendant-petitioner have preferred this revisional application under Section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay. 

5. Mr. A.H.M. Mushfiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appeared of the petitioner while Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite party No. 1. 

6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that on humanitarian ground, the defendant No.10 to the suit filed an application for time but the learned trial Court illegally 'ejected the same and without allowing adjournment for hearing fixed a date for argument. The learned Advocate further submits that I revisional Court during passing the impugned judgment and order also committed illegality and without applying his judicial mind affirmed the order of the trial Court. The learned Advocate also submits that the defendant-petitioner under compelling circumstance filed the adjournment petition but that the petition was rejected arbitrarily. 
7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the petitioner and submits that the learned trial Court as well as the I" revisional Court committed no illegality or irregularity in rejecting the time petition and thereafter in disallowing the Civil Revision being No.7 of 2010. The learned Advocate further submits that the defendant-petitioner during pre-emptory hearing of the original suit obtained as many as 24 (twenty four) adjournments which is unwarranted in law. Under the 
provisions laid down in order 17 Rule 1 (3) (4) of the Code of Civil Procedure as amended in the year 2003 the learned Court below was not in a position in allowing the adjournment prayer for more than three times. The trial Court allowed enough time and the defendant-petitioner on this ground or that ground took one after another adjournment of the hearing which has caused miscarriage of justice and when the matter is in the notice of the trial Court and the to revisional Court rightly rejected the adjournment prayer and affirmed the order of the trial Court under the specific provision of law. The learned Advocate in support of this contention referred two decisions of this Court reported in 30 DLR 313 and 12 BLT 284. The teamed Advocate lastly submits that there is no illegality or irregularity whatsoever and non-application of judicial mind in the matter and in absence of any illegality there is no scope to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed by the revisional Court.

8. Heard the teamed Advocates of both sides. perused the impugned judgment and order 4 along with the order of rejection of rime prayer passed by the trial Court on 09.03.2010 in Title Suit No.70 of 2008. I have also perused the order sheets marked Annexure-"C" and the adjournment prayer of the defendant-petitioner marked as Annexure-A.

9. On perusal of the connected papers it transpires that the original suit was fixed for further pre-emptory (F.P.H.) hearing on 09.03.2010 and on that date the defendant No.10 filed an application for adjournment supported by a Medical certificate. The date was fixed for cross-examination of the witnesses adduced from the side of the defendant Nos. -2 and 5. It further appears that the defendant-petitioner after getting summon-notice made his appearance and submitted written statement. From the observation of the 1" revisional Court it is noticed that the defendant-petitioner from his appearance dated 28.11.2006 till 09.03.2010 obtained about three years time after filing several applications. The 1st  revisional Court consulting the order sheet of the original case record inserted 24 dates of adjournments taken by the defendant petitioner and obviously decided the merit of the revisional application in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party therein. 

Under the ambit of Order 17 Rule I Sub-rule 3 no Court shall grant more than three adjournments to a party even with cost when the matter is fixed for pre-emptory hearing. Beside this; the provisions laid down in Order 17 Rule 4 read as follows: 

"Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code, the Court shall not grant any adjournment at the pre-emptory hearing stage and thereafter in suit at the instance of either party to the suit. 

Provided that if for ends of justice any adjournment is granted to a party under this Sub-rule, the Court shall direct that party to pay a cost of not less than two hundred taka and not more than one thousand taka to the other patty, within time to be specified by it, non compliance with which, by the plaintiff shall render the suit liable to be dismissed and, by the defendant shall render the suit liable to be disposed of ex-parte; Provided further that the Court shall not grant more than three adjournments to a party even with cost under the above provision." 

10. Granting of adjournment is no doubt a discretion vested in the Court as it evident from Order 17, rule I of the Code but the discretion must be exercised in a judicial and reasonable manner and not arbitrarily or capriciously, in which case it is no exercise of discretion, in the eye of law. Such arbitrarily exercise of discretion may tend to undermine the confidence and respect of the people in the administration of justice without which the judiciary cannot properly discharge its duties. The Courts should, therefore, be extremely careful in exercising the discretion vested in them and always keep in mind the legal maxim that 'justice must not only be done but must also appear to be done. 

11. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the submissions advanced hem the side of the learned Counsel for the opposite parties have substance. 

12. In the result, the Rule having no merit is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 10.07.2011 passed by the learned District Judge, Thakurgaon in Civil Revision No.7 of 2010, affirming the judgment and order dated 09.03.2010 passed by the leaned Assistant Judge, Haripur, Thakurgaon in Title Stilt No.70 of 2008 is hereby affirmed. 

13. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. 

14. Communicate the judgment and order at once.

End.

Mr. S.A.M. Mahbub Elahi, Advocate -- For the petitioner
No one appears -- For the opposite party
parties:

Versus

full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal .J:- This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the Order No. 102 dated 14.10.2009 and Order No. 103 dated 18.10.2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj in Artha Rin Money Execution Case No. 41 of 1999 should not be set-aside.

2. The material facts of the case as necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party No.1, Janata Bank, Fatullah Branch as plaintiff on 01.10.1996 instituted a suit being Artha Rin (Mortgage) Suit No. 43 of 1996 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj against the defendants praying for recovery of its outstanding loan amounting to Tk. 10,81,560/- along with 20% of interest till realisation of the unpaid amount. The defendants did not turn to contest the suit and thereupon, the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj took up the matter for ex-party hearing on 22.6.1997 and after ex-parte hearing was pleased to decree the suit against the defendants ex-parte in preliminary form by his order dated 22.6.1997 and directed the defendants to pay the decreetal amount of Tk. 1081560/- with 20% of interest till realisation within 45 days in default the plaintiff will have right to realise the decreetal amount by selling the suit property through Court. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat pursuant to the preliminary decree dated 22.6.1997 by his order dated 17.11.1997 prepared the final decree. The final decree was drawn up on 17.11.1997 by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj.

3. After obtaining the said ex-parte decree the decree-holder Bank preferred an application under Order 21 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for execution of the final decree. The said application was registered as Mortgage Execution Case No. 41 of 1997.

4. During the pendency of the said execution case the decree-holder-Bank on 18.8.2009 filed an application for issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. The learned Judge of the Adalat on considering of the materials on record by Order No. 102 dated 14.10.2009 issued warrant of arrest against the judgment debtor No. 2, Ansar Ali. Thereafter, the judgment-debtor Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for staying the execution case till disposal of the Title Suit No. 85 of 2009 pending before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd  Court, Narayanganj. The Adalat upon hearing the said application by its Order No. 103 dated 18.10.2009 rejected the application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 stating as follows:

“দায়িক কর্তৃক বিগত ৩০-৯-৯০ তারিখের স্থহিতাদেশ এর প্রার্থনায় আনীত দরখাস্ত অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ৩১ ধারার বিধান মতে উচ্চ আদালতের স্থগিতাদেশ ছাড়া স্থগিত রাখার বিধান না থাকায় নামঞ্জুর করা হইল।”

5. Under the above facts and circumstances of the case the judgment debtor-petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr. S. A. M. Mahbub Elahi, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in the course of argument after placing the impugned orders and other materials on record submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case the Artha Rin Adalat seriously erred in law in passing the impugned order without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. He next submits that the executing Court having failed to appreciate the simple legal aspect of the case the executing Court lost right to continue the execution case on 6.5.2008 when sale certificate was issued under section 33(5) and thereby entertained the application of the decree holder issuing warrant of arrest on 12.3.2009 and also on 14.10.2009 without following the provisions of section 51 read with Rule 37 of Order 21 of the Code of Civil procedure and rejected the application dated 30.9.2009 of the petitioner filed under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 with prayer for stay of the execution proceeding till disposal of the Title Suit No.85 of 2009 filed by the petitioner for setting-aside the ex-parte preliminary decree dated 24.6.97 and final decree dated 17.11.97 which resulted in the failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that no show cause notice was issued and sufficient opportunity of being heard was not given to the petitioners prior to passing the order issuing warrant of arrest as contemplated in the provision of section 51 read with order 21 Rule 37 of the Code of Civil Procedure which is mandatory provision of law and as such the impugned order relating to issuance of warrant of arrest suffers from patent illegality and the same is liable to be set aside.

7. Mr. Mahbuh Elahi, further argues that the ex-parte preliminary decree dated 24.6.97 and final decree dated 17.11.97 are not executable in as much as the decree is hit by non service of summons upon the defendants and for not filing the Artha Rin Mortgage Suit by competent person and it is also hit by the provisions of Order II, Rule I and Order 6 Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such justice demands to stay the execution proceedings till disposal of Title Suit No. 85 of 2009 filed by the petitioners.

8. Mr. Elahi, the learned Advocate finally on the point of maintainability of the revisional application against an interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat relying on the decisions reported in 1 BLC 179, 19 BLD 546, 48 DLR-57 and 44 DLR-340 as well as section 4 and 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 submits that as there is no provision for any appeal against an interlocutory order given by the Artha Rin Adalat the petitioners are not debarred to move an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

9. No one found present on behalf of the opposite parties to oppose the Rule.

10. We have heard the learned Advocate Mr. Elahi at length and perused the Revisional Application along with annexure including the cited decisions to the best of our ability. Now, to deal with the contentions raised by the learned Advocate before us it would be convenient for us to decide first of all the question of maintainability of the Revisional application against an interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat.

11. In the case of Sultana Jute Mills Ltd. and others Vs. Agrani Bank and others reported in 46 DLR(AD)174, it has been held that Revision under the Artha Rin Adalat Act is impliedly barred because the Act being a special legislation setting up special Court the remedies will follow as provided therein.

12. In the case of Hosne Ara Begum &another Vs Islami Bank Bangladesh and169reported in 5 MLR (AD) 290, it has been held that no Revision lies against an Interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat.

13. In the case of Iftekhar Afzal and another Vs. Pubali Bank Limited and others reported in 50 DLR 623, it has been held that interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat is not amenable to the revisional jurisdiction.

14. In the case of Belayet Hossain Vs Bank Indosuez reported in 50 DLR 431, it has been held that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain is a special legislature setting up Special Courts for prompt realisation of the loans by financial institution. A revisioinal application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against° any interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat is not maintainable.

15. In the case of Kazi Gowaherul Islam Vs. Standard Co-operative Credit Society Ltd. and another reported in 50 DLR 333, it has been held that as follows:

"Admittedly, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain is a special forum set up under a special legislation and the remedies will follow as provided in the Ain itself and it has been indicated by our Appellate Division that if there is any exclusion indicated in the Ain, as in section 6, it will include a remedy under the general law. So, on going through this decision of the Appellate Division, we hold that there is a complete ouster of jurisdiction of the high Court Division for interference under section 115 (1) of the Code of civil Procedure against any interlocutory matter or orders passed by the Adalat. In the two High Court division decisions as aforesaid, this decision of our Appellate Division has not been looked into. We, on perusal of this decision of our appellate Division, has not been looked into. We, on perusal of this decision of our appellate Division, are of the view that the impugned order is not revisable under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure as there is total bar under the Ain."

16. From a reading of the above quoted decisions, we are unable to accept the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners on the point of maintainability of the revisional application against an interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat rather we are led to hold that Revision under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against any interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat is not maintainable in law.

17. In the cited decisions namely the decisions reported in 1 BLC 179 and 48 DLR-57, it has been held by this Division that as there is no provision for any appeal against an interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat the petitioner is not debarred to move an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

18. In this connection to resolve the dispute whether the revisional application is maintainable against any interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, our Apex Court in the case of Md. Harun-Or-Rashid Vs. Pubali Bank Ltd. and others reported in 27 BLD (AD) 326 has been held as follows:

"Leave was granted to consider the submissions that the learned judges of the High Court Division were not justified in rejecting the writ petition summarily on the ground of maintainability of the writ petition against an interlocutory order of Artha Rin and as such the impunged jugment and order is liable to be set aside by this Court Furthermore, the learned Judges of the High Court Division failed to appreciate the decision in the case of Sultana Jute Mills Ltd. and others Vs. Agrani Bank reported in 14 BLD (AD) 196 wherein it is settled that writ petition is maintainable against an interlocutory order of the Artha Rin Adalat and in that view of the matter the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside by this Division. It is finally submitted that in view of some conflicting decisions of the High Court Division in the cases of Sonali Bank Vs. Ali Tannery, 48 DLR (HCD) 57, Kazi Gowaherul Islam Vs. Standard Co-operative, 50 DLR (HCD) 431 and Iftekher Afzal Vs Pubali Bank Ltd. 50 DLR (HCD) 623 an authorities pronouncement be made by this Division to resolve doubts which regards to the maintainability of writ petition or a revision against an interlocutory order of Artha Rin Adalat.

........................

........................

The learned Judges of the High Court  Division have held that since the decree  passed by the Artha Rin Adalat has been  made appealable to the High Court  Division Artha Rin Adalat is subordinate  to the High Court Division and in that  view of the matter the aggrieved party  can challenge any interlocutory order of the Artha Rin Adalat by invoking revisional jurisdiction under section 115  of the Code of Civil Procedure in view of Article 100 of the Constitution. This view is absolutely erratic and perverse.”

<u>19. From a plain reading of the above quoted decision we find a clear view of law stands today that no Revision lies against any interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat and that the conflicting decision of this Division namely in the case of Sonali Bank Vs. Ali Tannery reported in 48 DLR-57 on the point of maintainability to a revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against any interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat has been over ruled.</u>

20. Now let us examine, how far the learned Judge of the Adalat was justified in passing the impugned order No. 102 dated 14.10.2009 and order No. 103 dated 18.10.2009.

21. It appears that the decree-holder-Bank after selling the mortgage property through Court filed an application for issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtor for realization of its entire decreetal amount on 18.8.2009 stating as follows:

“উপরোক্ত মোকদ্দমায় ডিক্রিদার তপছিল বর্নিত সম্পত্তি নিলামে বিক্রি করিয়া দাইকগনের পা্ওনা পরিশোধ না হওয়ায় ডিক্রিদার ২-৩ নং দাইকগনের বিরুদ্ধে গ্রেফতারী পরওযানা ইস্যু করিবার দরখাস্ত প্রদান করিলে হুজুরাদালত ২-৩ নং দাইকগনের বিরুদ্ধে গ্রেফতারী পরওয়ানা ইস্যু করেন। কিন্তু পরবর্তীতে দাইকগন ডিক্রিদার ব্যাংকে টাকা জমা না দিয়া বিজ্ঞ আদালতকে ভুল বুঝাইয়া জামিন গ্রহন করেন। কাজেই দাইকগনের বিরুদ্ধে পুনরায় গ্রেফতারী পরওয়ানা ইস্যু করিয়া ২-৩ নং দাইকগনকে গ্র্রেফতার করিযা ডিক্রিদার ব্যাংকের পাওনা আদায়ের আদেশ হওয়া আবশ্যক।”

22. The Artha Rin Adalat upon considering the application as well as the attending facts and circumstances of the case by its order No. 102 dated 14.10.2009 issued warrant of arrest against the judgment debtor No. 2.

23. In the case of Provat Kumar Das Vs171Agrani Bank and another reported in 15 BLC (AD) 113, wherein our Apex Court affirmed the view of the High Court Division that the Adalat is empowered to pass an order of warrant of arrest/civil imprisonment directly when no auction sale is possible to be held for any reason.

<u>24. On an analysis of the impugned order vis-a-vis the application for issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtor-petitioners filed on 18.8.2009 as evidenced by `Annexure-H' to the revisional application and the decisions reported in 15 BLC(AD) 113 and 15 BLC-180, we find no flaw in the reasoning’s of the Adalat. The learned Judge of the Adalat appears to have considered all the legal aspects of the case in passing the impugned order of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtor No. 2.</u>

25. Now, in remains for us to consider that how far the learned Judge of the Adalat was justified in rejecting the application filed by the judgment-debtors for staying all further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of Title Suit No. 85 of 2009.

26. The Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is special law, the legislature with intent to prompt realisation of the loan given by financial institution by applying special method enacted the special law namely the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Now, keeping in mind the settled proposition of law let us proceed to examine at the relevant provision in respect to pass an order to stay the proceedings of the execution case.

27. Section 31 of the Ain, 2003 reads as follows:

“জারীর কার্যক্রমের স্থগিতাদেশ অর্থ ঋণ আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত কোন আদেশ বা ডিক্রির বিরুদ্ধে আপীল বা রিভিশন উচ্চতর আদালতে দায়ের করা হইলে উহা স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে জারীর কার্যধারা স্থগিত করিবে না উচ্চতর আদালত সুস্পষ্ঠভাব তদুদ্দেশ্যে স্থগিতাদেশ প্রদান করিলেই কেবল জারীর কার্যধারা তদঅনুযায়ী স্থগিত হইবে।”

28. From a reading of the above quoted section, it transpires that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 does not empower the Artha Rin Adalat to pass an order to stay the proceedings of the execution case whatsoever. Our view therefore is that the Artha Rin Adalat rightly on assigning sound reason rejected the application for stay of the execution case till disposal of Title Suit No. 85 of 2009 by its order dated 18.10.2009. The second impugned order dated 18.10.2009 is also well founded in law. No interference is, therefore, called for.

29. We, therefore, do not find any substance in the submissions made by Mr. S.A. M. Mahbub Elahi, the learned Advocate for the petitioners.

30. In view of our discussion made in the foregoing paragraphs and the principles laid down in the decisions reported in 46 DLR(AD) 174, 5 MLR(AD) 290, 27 BLD(AD) 326, 15 BLC(AD) 113 and 15 BLC-180 by now it is clear that the instant Rule must fail.

31. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The Order No. 102 dated 14.10.2009 and Order No.103 dated 18.10.2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj in Money Execution Case No. 41 of 1999 are hereby maintained. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

32. Communicate this judgment at once.

End.

caseno:
CIVIL REVISION NO 114 OF 1988 (Syllaet)
CIVIL REVISION NO. 4873 OF 1991 (Dhaka)
lawyer:
Mr. J.N. Dev for the Petitioner 
Mr. H.N. Nandi with Mr. T. K. Dutta for the opposite party
parties:
Md. Rajiuddin Chowdhury ------ petitioner
VERSUS
Suruj Ali ------ Opposite party
full_judgment:
ABU SAYEED AHAMED, J: Present Rule at the instance of plaintiff against the judgment of affirmance in a suit for possession on redemption of mortgage. Plaintiff Md. Rajiuddin Chowdhury transferred 54 acres agricultural land for Tk. 700/- to the defendant Suruj Ali, by kabala executed on 10.7.49 (Ext.1). Transferee executed an Ekrarnama on 13.7.49 (Ext.2). Both the documents were registered on 7.11.49. Transferee agreed to recovery the land as per terms of ekrarnama if consideration money was paid back within 6 years. After promulgation of President Orders 88 of 1972 (Called Second Amendment Order), 136 of 1972 and 24 of 1973, on an application by the transferor claiming that the transaction was an usfructuory mortgage in case 2 of 1973 the local Circle Officer (Revenue) on 24.11.1973 granted redemption and directed the transferee to deliver possession of the land to the transferor in view of the provision Section 95A (4) (6) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (which shall hereinafter the called the Act) as amended by the said President Orders.

2. Opposite party then filed Title Suit 71 of 1974 which was decreed on 31.12.76 declaring that the order passed by the Circle Officer was without jurisdiction. Petitioner thereafter instituted the present Title Suit 83 of 1989 for possession of the suit 'land on redemption and claiming the transfer as a complete usufructory mortgage and for further declaration that the judgment and decree of the Title suit 71 of 1974 are illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. Both the courts below relying on the decision of Bangladesh Vs. Hazi Abdul Ghani, 32 DLR (AD) 233, dismissed the suit on the finding that the transfer of the suit land was an out and out sale, the Ekrarnama, containing condition to recovery, being a separate document, it was not embraced within the provision of Section 95A of the Act, as amended by the President Order 88 and 136 of 1972, the transaction was not alive and it was a past and closed transaction as time limit for reconveyance was 6 (six) years from the date of Ekrarnama, being 13.10.49 and in view of the decision of Title Suit 71 of 1974, both the courts below held that the present suit is barred by principles of resjudicata and limitation.

3. To my mind question involves in this matter in dispute is whether the transaction is a complete usufractury mortgage as contemplated under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Act XXVIII of 1951) as amended by President Orders 88 and 136 of 1972 and if so whether the transaction in question is a past and closed one and whether if can be declared as redeemed, as prayed for by plaintiff-petitioner or whether it can be redeemed by a separate suit within 60 years. "Complete usufractuory mortgage" has been defined in Section 2, Sub-section 6 of the Act as follows:-

"'Complete usufructuary mortgage means a transfer by a tenant of the right of possession in any land for the purpose of securing the payment of money or the return of grain advanced or to be advanced by way of loan upon the condition that the loan, with all interest thereon, shall be deemed to be extinguished by the profits arising from the land during the period of the mortgage."

Section 95 of the Act provides that a raiyat could not enter into any kind of usufractuory mortgage other than the complete usufractuary mortgage. The Transfer of Property Act so far as mortgage  of raiyati holding is concerned (Section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act, Act IV of 1882) is thus displaced (32 DLR (AD) 233, para 5.

4. In Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885, Section 260 was inserted by amending Act IV of 1928 which came into force on 22.2.29 with object to protect a Raiyat so that no Mahazan could keep a raiyat out of his land for more than 15 years on the plea of non-payment of petty loan. The amending Act IV of 1928 of Bengal Tenancy Act introduced a new definition of Complete usufractuary mortgage by section 3(3) of the the Bengal Tenancy Act. Definition of complete usufractuary mortgage, is same both in Bengal Tenancy Act and in State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which has been quoted above. Said 15 years was reduced to 7 years by Ordinance No. XXI of 1969.

5. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act after amendment by President Orders 88 and 136 of 1972, stands as follows:-

"95A. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, either by  way of an out and out sale with an  agreement to reconvey, or where the transferor received from the transfer any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion of share thereof for a spaced period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufrctuary  mortgage for period not exceeding seven  clears and the provisions of section 95  shall apply to such transfer whether  made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition  and  Tenancey (Second Amendment) Order 1972 (See page 239) left hand column of 32 DLR (AD) ease of Bangladesh Vs. Hazi Abdul Ghani,

Thus it can be safely and clearly found that the transfer involved in the instant case is embraced within the nature and definition of complete usufructuary mortgage as envisaged by section 95A of the Act. According to the provision of Section 95A of the Act, as quoted above, the transfer in the instant case is a complete usufructuary mortgage although it is a sale with a condition to reconvey and although it took place, before the commencement of the Second Amendment of the Act, by President order 88 and 136 of 1972 and 24 of 1973. In the decision given by the Full Bench of the Appellant Division in the case of Abu Bakkar Vs. Nazir Ahmed, reported in 34 DLR(AD) 237 it has been held in para 5 and 6 as under:-

"Para 5. But on perusual of the judgment of the High Court Division it is found that learned Advocate of both the parties who appeared there were confused between the period of subsistence of a usufructuary mortgage and the period of limitation in the case of a suit for redemption of a mortgaged land. The maximum period for which a usufructuary mortgage can be entered into was fifteen years under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, but by ordinance No. XXI of 1969 section 95 was amended and thereby the maximum period for usufructuary mortgage was reduced to seven years. And unless earlier redeemed by repayment of the consideration a mortgager acquires right to redemption on the expiry of the maximum period of seven yeas, and if the mortgage does not voluntarily restore possession of the land to the corgagor, the latter may file a suit for redemption within a period of 60  wars from the date of accrual of his right of redemption. In this case the suit of redemption and as such it is not barred by limitation."

Para 6: Section 95 has been again amended by the President's order no. 88 of 1972 with eject from 3 August, 1972, but this  amendment did not touch the period of usufructuary mortgage which is still 7 years  nor did it affect the period of limitation for  redemption suit which is 60 year. The amendment relates to two new provision. One is that on the expiry of the period of a mortgage the mortgagee does not restore possession of the land to the mortgagor, then the Sub-divisional. Magistrate shall, on an application by the mortgagor, restore possession to the mortgagor by evicting the mortgages. In other words, for getting back possession of a cortgaged land the mortgagor need not file any, redemption suit, but may get quick remedy by an application to the sub-divisional Magistrate. The other provision in the amendment Is that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law in force, anti transfer of a land by  an out and out sale with a condition for reconveyance shall be deemed to be a  complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding 7 years on the expiry of which the mortgagor may get back possession Magistrate application to the Sub-divisional Magistrate....

Now I venture to find that the decision given in the case of 34 DLR(AD) 237 is a shield and has given a protection to the petitioner to bring the transfer of his suit land within the arena of section 95 and 95A of the Act and within the ambit of the definition of complete usufructuary mortgage for the avowed purpose of president Orders 88 and 136 of 1972 and 24 of 1973 and the petitioner is entitled to file a suit for redemption within 60 years from the date of expiry of the stipulated period as was stipulated in the deed to reconvey and can recover possession of the suit land on redemption. My considered view is that the courts below under misconception of law and due to misinterpretation of the decision in the case of 32 DLR (AD) 233 have dismissed the suit of the petitioner and they have found an inapplicable blanket embargo against the case of the petitioner in 32 DLR(AD) 233's case. I find that the present case gets it's life and strength in the decision of that case (See para 5 of 32 DLR(AD) 233).

6. In view of the discussions above, the submissions of Mr. H.N.Nandi, the learned Counsel for the opposite party that the transaction is not an usufructuary mortgage as provided under section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act and the transaction being an out and out sale with condition to reconvey and since the plaintiff did not come with a suit of specific performance of contract within the limitation as was affixed in the Ekranama the present suit is barred by limitation and consequently it does not come within the purview of the section 95A of the Act to cover by the President Orders 88 and 136 of 1972 and it is a past and closed transaction as found in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Haji Abdul Ghani, 32 DLR(AD) 233, have no legal force or leg to stand and are repelled have already found that the mortgage as defined in the transfer of property act as to Raiyati holding has already been displaced after commencement of President order 88 and 136 of 1972 which have introduced section 95A of the Act (See para 5 of 32 DLR(AD) 233). Since I am convinced to find and hold that the transfer in question is a complete usufructory mortgage. So the suit is not barred by limitation as held by the courts below. In this case limitation will be governed by Article 148 of the Limitation Act which is 60 years.

<u>7. Title suit 71 of 1976 of the contesting defendant was a suit for declaration that the order passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue) on 24.11.1973 in Redemption Case 2 of 1973, is illegal, without jurisdiction and for permanent injunction. Present suit is for redemption of mortgage and for khas Possession and for declaration that the decree passed on 31.12.76 in Title Suit 71 of 1976 is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. Not only cause of action and Subject matter are different but also issues are completely different. So there was no scope for final decision by the former court in respect of the present subject matter, pending for decision in the present suit. Therefor I find that the decision in Title Suit 71 of 1976 is not bar, by resjudicata, in deciding the present suit. The decision in title suit 71 of 1976 is not a legal decision. So it is not binding upon the plaintiff. Mr. J.N. Dev, the learned Counsel for the petitioner pursuaded me to go through the decision in the case of Mathura Prasad Sarjoo Jaiswal and others Vs. Dossibai N.B.Jeejeebhoy, AIR 1971(SC) 2355 in support of his submission that the present suit will not be barred by resjudicata. In that case, their Lordships have opined in para 9 on resjudica as follows:-</u>

<u>"A question relating to the jurisdiction of a court cannot be deemed to have been finally determined by an erroneous decision of the Court. If by an erroneous interpretation of the status the Court holds that it has no jurisdiction, the question would not, in our judgment, operate as resjudicata. Similarly by an erroneous decision if the court assumes jurisdiction which it does not posses under the statute the question cannot operate as resjudicata between the same parties, whether the cause of action in the subsequent litigation is the same or otherwise."</u>

<u>I find that the decision lends strong support to the petitioner to overcome the barrier of resjudicata as found by the courts below in dismissing his suit.</u>

8. For the reasons above, I hold that the courts below committed illegality in arriving at their decisions in dismissing the suit of the petitioner which resulted occasioning failure of justice. So I am inclined to interfere.

9. The result, therefor is, that the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgments and decrees of the courts below are set aside. The suit of the plaintiff-petitioner being Title suit 83 of 1989 is decreed declaring that the mortgage has been redeemped and the plaintiff is entitled to get khas possession of the suit land by executing the decree against the defendant and that the decree passed in Title Suit 71 of 1976 is no more binding upon the petitioner.

10. No order as to costs.

11. Send down the records of the case to the courts below immediately.

End.

lawyer: Mr. A. B. M. Khairul Hoque with Ms. Snigdha Hoque .... for the petitioner. Mr. A. F. Hasan Arif with Mr. Borhanuddin  for the Oppo. party.
parties:
Sonali Bank ------  Petitioner
Versus
M/s. Ali Tannery Ltd. and others  ------ Opp. Parties.
full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam, J: This revisional application at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against an order dated 12.11.91 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and 2nd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong, in Money Suit No. 52 of 1988, disallowing the plaintiff's application for rejection of counter claim of the defendants. 

2. This facts as are relevant for disposal of the application may be stated as follows. 
The Sonali Bank, Agrabad Branch, Chittagong filed the aforesaid money suit for realisation of an amount of Tk. 1,98,48,632.70 being the principal amount of loan including interest as on 31.1.88 with a further prayer of pendent elite interest @ 20% per annum

on and from the date of filing the suit i ill realisation of the decretal dues with cost and other charges. Ultimately on 31.10.90 the case was transferred to the 1st Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong, by virtue of amendment of section 9 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. 

3. The defendants opposite parties appeared and filed a joint written statement on 29.8.91. In the said written statement they admitted the loan but disputed the claims of the plaintiffs and also made a counter. Claim of Tk. 2,61,04,706.91 against the plaintiff 
petitions on different counts as damages and compensation.  

4. The plaintiff petitioner on 19.10.91 filed an application in the trial court for rejecting the prayer of counter Claim on the ground that Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 empowers only Bank and same other specified financial Institutions to institute suit for recovery of Loan and since the defendants do not answer the Said description they cannot file a counter claim in Artha Rin Adalat. The said application dated 19:10.91 was heard by the trial court on 12.11.91 and the said application of the plaintiff was rejected by the trial court holding that the counter claim was made under the relevant provisions of the code of Civil procedure which is applicable in the 
proceedings of Artha Rin Adalat. In the present Rule the plaintiff petitioner call in question the legality and propriety of the said order of the trial court. 

5. Mr. Khairul Haque, the learned advocate, appears of the petitioner and submits that Artha. Rin Adalat is a special court set up for special purpose of speedy recovery of loans by the Banks and specified financial institutions only and the Artha Rin Adalat has no jurisdiction to adjudicates the claim of any other person. He further submits that Artha Rin Adalat has jurisdiction to adjudicate in the matter of recovery of loans of the aforesaid institutions only 
and not in respect of any other kinds of claim which does not come within the definition of "V I" (Loan) as defined in section 2 (kha) of the Act and as such the counter claim is not entertainable. 

6. Mr. Hasan Ali, the learned advocate, who appears for the defendant, opposite parties, submits that Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990, hereinafter called the 'Act' is a procedural law and it does not create any forum i.e. Artha Rin Adalat has got no independent it existence of its own. He draws our attention to section 3 of the Act and submits that the provisions of the Act is complementary and not derogatory to other law and as such section 3 if read with section 5(4) 
and 5(5) of the Act will show that Artha Rin Adalat is an ordinary Civil court as contemplated in the civil procedure code and the civil procedure code is applicable in its entirety to the proceedings of the Artha Rin Adalat unless they are repugnant to the express provisions of the 
Act. He further argues by referring to order 37 of the code of Civil procedure and submits that even the civil procedure code also provides special procedure on negotiable Instrument and the spell procedure has been extended by the A& arid therefore, the Artha Rin Adalat is very much a civil court under the civil courts Act.1887, as well as under the civil procedure code. His next submission is that section 7 of the Act by providing special procedure for appeal simply decrecte the scope of order 41 and section 94 of the civil procedure code. His final argument is that section 6 of the Act provides that the proceeding, Order, Judgment and decree of Artha Rin Adalat shall not be called in question before any court or authority same as provided by section 7 of the Act and as such section 6 prohibits revision to the High Court Division. 

7. Before we take up the above noted points for consideration it would be pertinent to note that the Act has come up for consideration in various cases in the past before this court as well as before the Appellate Division. It appears that all the points that have been against before us have already been considered in different CP.SDS except the last point. To cut the matter short it may be stated that it has already been held by the Appellate Division in the case of Md. Zahirul Islam Vs. National Bank Ltd. and others in CPSLA No. 251 and 318 of 1993 reported in 1994 (11) BLT SC (AD) 23 that Artha Rin Adalat is a special forum created by a special law for adjudication of suits which can be filed by a Bank or a financial Institution for recovery of its loan. 

8. Similarly in the case of M/S. MAC Proprietor, Mahtabuddin Chowdhury and another Vs Agrani Bank reported in 14 BLD (1994) 195, a Division Bench of the High Court Division after considering different provisions of the Act held that this Artha Rin Adatat. Ain is a special taw under which courts were constituted with their is own forum of appeal. So, by way of interpreting the provisions of Sub-sections (4) and (5) of Section 5, it cannot be found that this is an ordinary 
civil court for all pretrial purposes and all the provisions of the code of civil procedure a e applicable in the proceeding." 

9. Finally in the case of Sultan Alam S.A. Badal Vs. Rupali Bank reported in 46 DLR 292 this bench after considering the provisions of the Act held that the nature and function of Artha Rin Adalat coupled with its power and authority clearly indicate that it is a special forum of limited jurisdiction and not an ordinary civil court and can not review its own judgment under the provision of order 47 rule I of the civil procedure Code. 

10 . From the finding and observations of the aforesaid cases it is clear that the submissions of Mr. Arif that the Act did not create a forum or that the Artha Rin Adalat is an ordinary civil court and that the court precaution cald applies in its entirety to the proceeding of the said court is negatived. 

11. Now let us consider the final submission of Mr. Aril that a revision does not lie from an order of the Artha Rin Adalat let us examine and see if his submission has got any substance. It may be stated that in construing the word "final" in many decisions of the Superior Courts of this sub continent, it has been held that the word "final" does not necessarily take away revisionary power as "final" means not appealable but open to revision. In considering the scope of Section 115 of the Civil procedure Code, the full Bench of the Madras High Court in the case of PARTHASARADHL NADU  VS KOTESWARA RAO, 47 MAD 369 F.B.) observed" It is further argued that the fact that the decision of this Judge is, by Section 57 of the Act Local Boards Act and by the rules, final, Precludes any revision. There is really no authority adduced in support of that proposition and in my Judgment it would be quite contrary to the whole object and intention of section 115, Civil procedure code so to hold. The section only applies where there is no appeal. This decision has been followed in 1950 MAD. 730. 

12. In construing the word "final" which occurs in section 29 (6) of the East Bangal premises Rent control. Act it was held that the word means that the order of Rent controller was subject to the result of an appeal to the District Judge, final. It does not take away the 
jurisdiction of the High Court to interfere with the District Judges order under section 115 civil procedure Code. 

13. In considering section 43 of the WAKFS Ord. 1962, the Supreme Court in the case of Amir Sultan Vs. Md. K. Alam, 29 D. L. R. (SC) 295 observed that Though his decision has been made final, which precludes any further appeal front his decision, such finality as attaches there 
to does not oust the revisional power of the High Court, "In interpreting similar provision as embodied in Article 29 (A) of the local Govt. Union Parishad Ord. 1983, the Appellate Division in 38 D.L.R. (AD) 172 held that the District Judge acting as an election appellate Tribunal is not a persons designate but a court subordinate to the High Court Division. 

14. It has been held in a number of decisions that the Artha Rin Adalat is not as Ordinary civil court but a special forum of Limited Jurisdiction. The question, therefore, arises whether an 
order passed by a court of special Jurisdiction is revisable by this U/S. 115 C.P.C. we can resolve this question easily if we can find as answer to the question is the Artha Rin Adalat a court subordinate to the High Court Division. In deciding this issue with regard to special statutes the superior courts of this Subcontinent have formulated certain principles. If appeal lies from a special tribunal to the High Court then that special tribunal is subordinate to the High Court. Similarly if the special court is under the administrative control of the High Court, 
it is also subordinate i.o the High Court. If we examine the provisions of the Act we 
find that section 7 provides that an appeal shall lie against a judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat to the High Court Division Section 4(2) of the Act provides that the Judges of the Artha Rin Adalat will be appointed from amongst the Subordinate Judge, in consultation 
with the Supreme Court. Rule framed under the Act provides that the Artha Rin Adalat will be under the Administrative control of the Supreme Court. It has been held in one case that if the court is one from which an appeal lies to the High Court though in certain specified .cases, 
then the court is subject to the appellate jurisdiction of the High Court and that is sufficient to attract the power of superintendence conferred on the High Court. Besides Article 109 of the 
constitution provides that High Court Division shall have superintendence and control over all courts subordinate to it and Article 114 provides, "There shall be in addition to the Supreme Court such courts subordinate there to as may be established by law." So it is crystal clear 
that Artha Rin Adalat though a special court, is never the less a court subordinate to the High Court Division and is, therefore, amenable to the revisional Jurisdiction of the High Court Division. So, we find that this revisional application filed by the petitioner is maintainable. 

15. We have already held earliar that the Civil procedure code is not applicable in its entirety in a proceeding before the Artha Rin Adalat. Mr. Arif submitted that since the application of order 8 of the Civil procedure Code has not been barred by the Act, the Artha Rin Adalat is competent to entertain a counter claim under the provision of order 8, Rule 6(1) of the civil procedure code. If we examine the scheme and the other provisions of the Act we find that it is only the financial Institutions as defined in section 2(Ka) which are entitled to institute a case In the Artha Rin Adalat for recovery of loan as defined in section 2 (KHA) of the Act and no other person or institution is authorised to file a case before the Artha Rin Adalat. So, if a defendant in a Artha Rin Adalat case is allowed to set up counter claim or set of he will be allowed to do a thing indirectly which he cannot do directly and this will run counter to the intent and purpose of the Act. Moreover, the right to set up a plea of counter claim is a substantive right and not a matter of more procedure. We have examined the provisions of the Act and there is no provision for making counter claim by defendant. The learned Artha Rin Adalat by entertainting the counter claim of the defendants opposite parties has acted in excess of to jurisdiction. 

16. There is yet another aspect of the case. Even if it were held that the Civil procedure code is applicable in the instant case then also the trial court acted illegally and without jurisdiction in as much as the counter claim raised by the defendant do not come within the preview of Rule 6 of Order 8 as the sum claimed by way of damages is not an ascertained amount. 
17. Mr. Hasan Arif, the learned advocate, previously took adjournments to place before us a decision of the Appellate Division. To day he has place before us the Judgment and order dated 13.6.94 of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Appeal No. 7 of 1994. This decision does not help the learned Advocate rather it goes against him as it has been held there in that an Artha Rin Adalat can not entertain any set off or counter claim in a suit tried by it. 

18. After a review of the aforesaid decisions and the provisions of the Act we find that the submissions of Mr. Khairul Hoque have got substance and accordingly the Rule is made absolute. The impugned order dated 12.11.91, so far it relates to the rejection of the application dated 19.10.91 is set aside and the application dated 19.10.91 filed by the plaintiff is allowed and the counter claim is rejected. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case there will be no order as to cost.

End.
