full_judgment:
Mr. Mir Hashmat Ali, J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Order No. 15 dated 03.02.2005 and decree dated 10.02.2005 passed by the learned Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 2, Bagerhat in Artha Rin Case No. 33 of 2004 whereby the case was disposed of on the basis of the report submitted by the settler and issued a certificate under section 22(10) of the Artha Rin Adalat  Ain, 2003 in favour of the plaintiff Bank vide Annexure-'A' and 'A-1' should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

2. The Respondent No. 2 as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Case No. 33 of 2004 against the defendant-petitioner herein after called the defendant for realization loan of Tk. 9,77,484/- only. 

3. The Artha Rin Suit No. 33 of 2004 was taken up for exparte disposal on 03.02.2005 and exparte decreed the suit, accordingly on 10.02.21305 decree was signed. The plaintiff decree holder started execution Case No.58 of 2005 before the Artha Rin Adalat and Joint District Judge, Bagerhat on 27.06.2005. 4. The plaintiff case in short is that, M/s. Barishal Store a business firm and the petitioner-defendant is the Proprietor of the said business firm, The Janata Bank granted a C.C. Loan of Tk. 8,00,000/- vide Sanction letter No. অগ্রীম/সি.সি/৪৫/০১ dated 08.08.2001. As a security for the C.C. loan the petitioner executed different deeds and security, the ' petitioner executed a mortgage deed in respect of land described in the schedule and ' the petitioner re-paid the same in time and thereafter the Janata Bank again granted a C.C. loan of Tk. 8,00,000/- vide Memo No. অগ্রীম/সি.সি/৪৮/০২ dated 17.06.2002 and the defendant received of Tk. 10,12,157/-. Though the petitioner obtained profit from the business but he did not pay up the loan. Though the plaintiff requested for payment of loan along with interest up to 17.03.2004 A to the tune of Tk.9,77,848/- only. The plaintiff served legal notice but the defendant does not pay and hence the Artha Rin Suit. 

5. The defendant-petitioner appeared and submitted written statement on 30.08.2004 stating that earlier loan has already been paid and adjusted in time but the plaintiff with ill motive continued the said loan in this account. It was further asserted in the written statement that on 17.06.2002 C.C. 4; loan was granted up to Tk. 8,00,000/- but the plaintiff most illegally stated that the defendant withdrawn Tk. 10,12,157/-. The trial Court after framing the issues, suo-moto fixed on 22.09.2004 for effecting compromise vide order dated 13.09.2004 and appointed the teamed Advocate for that effect and the next date was fixed on 24.10.2004 for report.) The defendant subsequently came to know on 17.07.2005 that decree has been passed on 03.02.2005 under Section 44 of the Artha Rio Adalat AM, 2003. Consequently, the defendant-petitioner on 08.08.2005 filed an application r, under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Aim 2003 for setting aside the said decree dated 03.02.2005 along with an application on the ground that a fraud has been committed in the order dated 03.02.2005 and as such the duty of the trial Court Is to set aside the same but without hearing the said application or without disposing of the said application started execution proceeding. It was further stated though the application under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain has been filed before the Artha Rin Adalat but no order has been passed by the said Adalat. 

6. Being aggrieved, the defendant-petitioner filed instant writ petition and obtained Rule. 

7. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that no notice was served upon the petitioner by the learned Advocate for effecting compromise. He further submits that learned Advocate for the petitioner obtained a signature under a verification for other purpose but such verification has been used as compromise petition. He further submits that according to Sub section 4 of Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 there should be a meeting between the parties and execute an agreement for effecting compromise and after the execution of the agreement the settler shall submit a report along with the agreement. Both the parties required to be signed in the said agreement and the learned Advocates of both the parties should also signed as witness to the compromise agreement and -after the said compromise the decree will be passed according to Order 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But in the instant case the compromise petition annexure-W to the writ petition shows that no agreement was effected and both the parties has not signed in the said report of the settler and none of the plaintiffs has been signed in the said report and as such the said report can not be construed as an agreement having under the term and conditions of agreement. He further submits that ,176710 which was mentioned in the said report of the settler shows that the petitioner has signed in the said paper in the chamber of his learned Advocate not before the settler and as such a fraud has been committed upon the petitioner. He further submits that even if for argument sake a settlement has been made; the decree if any should be passed in accordance with Order 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But in the instant case decree has been passed under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM. He further submits that under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM ad-interim order can be passed but not a decree and as such the order passed by Artha Rin Adalat on 03.02.2005 is an order but not a decree and as such it is amenable under the writ jurisdiction. He further submits that no notice was served upon the defendant-petitioner by the settler. But the plaintiff in connivance with the learned Advocate for the petitioner fraudulently used the ,137,105 Of the petitioner executed for other purpose in the chamber of the learned Advocate petitioner. He further submits that the defendant-petitioner never appeared before the settler as no notice was issued and served upon him by the settler. He further submits that at the time of passing the alleged order/ decree; Rule 3 of order 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure has not been observed and complied with; which indicate that the agreement which may form part of the decree is not a lawful order. In the instant case the decree is not lawful and that the Court below violated the mandatory provisions of Section 22 and 24 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. He further submits that for effecting compromise according to the Section 24 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain; the Board of directors of the plaintiff-Bank should pass a resolution to that effect but in the instant case no such resolution has been taken by the Artha Rin Adalat is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Government of Bangladesh-Vs-Ministry of Home Affairs and another passed in Sao mom Rule No.02 of 2007, the case of Hossain All Khan-Vs-Firoza Begum reported in 21 DLR-9. He further submits that the order dated 03.02.2005 is a misconceived order and under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain no decree can be passed and as such decree is not lawful decree and amenable to the writ jurisdiction. He further submits that after the order dated 03.02.2005 the petitioner filed an application under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM but the Court below passed no order though the Adalat received the application. 

8. Mr. Mamunur Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent-Bank submits that since the decree has been passed against the respondent-petitioner the remedy lies in filing the appeal against such decree and no writ petition is maintainable even if the decree is illegal. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Zahirul Islam - Vs National Bank Ltd. And others reported in 46 DLR (AL))- 191, the case of Gazi M. Towfic-VsAgrani Bank and others reported in 54 DLR(AD)-6, the case of - Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) Vs- Artha Rin Adalat AM and others reported in 59 DLR (AD)-6. 

9. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties and considered the writ petition and the annexures thereof. 

10. It appears from the writ petition that Respondent No. 2, Janata Bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Case No. 33 of 2004 before the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 2, Bagerhat for realization of Tk. 10,12,157/- against the defendant-petitioner stating that the defendant-petitioner took loan against C.C. Account No. 45 of 2001 amounting to Tk.8,00,000/-. At the time of taking loan the defendant-petitioner executed mortgage deed in favour of the Bank on 12.04.2001 and 19.04.2001. Subsequently, after payment of entire dues the defendant-petitioner again prayed for loan and the plaintiff-respondent No. 2 again on 17.06.2002 vide Memo No. অগ্রীম/সি.সি/৮৪/০২ granted joint C.C. loan of Tk. 8,00,000/-. The plaintiff demanded repayment of the loan. At the time of filing of the Artha Rin Suit; the entire claim was Tk. 10,12,175. It appears that the defendant-petitioner appeared and submitted written statement. The Artha Rin Adalat on 13.09.2004 fixed the date for compromise between the parties and Advocate Shapan Kumar Deb was engaged as settler and 24.10.2004 was fixed for report. But on 24.10.2004 no report was submitted before the Artha Rin Adalat. Next date was fixed on 24.11.2004. The settler, the learned Advocate filed an application for adjournment. The prayer was allowed and the date was fixed on 30.11.2004. On 30.11.2004 the settler learned Advocate filed an application for adjournment. The prayer was allowed and on 06.01.2005 was fixed for filing report in Court. On 06.01.2005 the settler learned Advocate took no steps and the trial Court found that the settler failed to make any compromise and fixed on 03.02.2005 for hearing of the suit, On the date fixed for hearing of the- suit on 03.02.2005 the settler submitted a report, The Artha Rin Adalat accepted the report and decreed the suit under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain according, to the report of  the settler. ৪৪. অন্তবর্তীকালীন আদেশ।- (১) অর্থঋণ আদালত,মামলার সঠিক ও পরিপূর্ণ বিচার ও ন্যায় বিচারের প্রয়োজনেএবং বিচার কার্যক্রমের অপব্যবহার প্রতিরোধকল্পে যেরুপঅন্তবর্তীকালীন আদেশ প্রদান করা সংগত মনে করিবে,সেরুপ অন্তবর্তীকালীন আদেশ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে ৷
(২) উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, এই আইনেরঅধীনে কোন আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত কোন অন্তবর্তীকালীনআদেশকে উচ্চতর কোন আদালতে আপীল বা রিভিশনআকারে বিতর্কিং করা যাইবে না।
(৩) ঊপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও, কোন পক্ষ ধারা ৪১এর অধীন দায়েরকৃত আপীলে এইরুপ কোন বিষয় যুক্তিহিসাবে গ্রহন করিতে পারিবে, যাহা ঊপরি-উল্লিখিত বিধানেরকারনে বিতর্কিত করা যায় নাই, এবং আপীল আদালতঐরুপ বিষয় বিবেচনায় গ্রহন করিয়া ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থেউপযুক্ত যে কোন আদেশ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে ৷

And as such we find that no decree can be passed under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM. The Artha Rin Adalat most erroneously and illegally passed the decree and Section 44 does not empower the Adalat to pass any decree against any person. It has been held in the case of Mir Motiur Rahman Zihadi -Vs- Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail and another reported in 15 BLT(AD)-267, that A judgment-debtor is not competent to challenge the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in writ jurisdiction unless the judgment and decree of the Adalat is without jurisdiction or in other words coram non judice or outcome of fraud committed on Court and that also suffers from 'malafide. It has been held in the case of Md. Arfan Uddin Akand and another -Vs- Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Gazipur and another reported in 15 BLT(HCD)-343. 

"Considering the decisions referred above and discussions made herein above, we are of the view that if the Adalat passed any order, which is wholly without jurisdiction, not in excess of jurisdiction, then despite of the fact that the law provided forum for appeal, the petitioner cannot be debarred from availing the jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. Because the question of jurisdiction of the Court goes to the very root of the matter brought before it and when the Court does not have any Jurisdiction to see, everything done subsequent thereto shall fall through and the Court which has got no jurisdiction to pass such order over the matter shall not go into the merit of the matter as decided in the case of the Managing Director, Ripple Bank Ltd. And others -Vs-Tafazal Hossain and others reported in 44 DLR(AD)-260." 

12. It has also been held in the case of Hossain Ali Khan -Vs- Firoza Begum reported in 21 DLR-9, that "Rule 3 Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure clearly indicates that the agreement which may form part of the decree must be lawful and if it is contrary to law, a court cannot pass a decree in accordance with such an agreement." 

13. We have observed that the report submitted by the settler is not an agreement in accordance with law as both the parties has not signed in the agreement and such an agreement cannot be form part of the decree according to order 3 of Rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. No body dispute that against the decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat the remedy lies an appeal. But in the instant case the Artha Rin Adalat passed the decree on an unlawful agreement and that the decree was passed under Section 44 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and as such, such decree is without jurisdiction and as such the judgment and decree dated 03.02.2005 is amenable under the writ jurisdiction. 

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, we find substance in the instant Rule. 

In the result, the rule is made absolute without any other as to the cost. 

14. The impugned Order No. 15 dated 03.02.2005 and the decree thereof dated 10.02.2005 passed by Artha Rin Adalat, Court No.2, Bagerhat in Artha Rin Case No. 33 of 2004 is declared to have been made and passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. However, the suit is remanded to the Trial Court for fresh trial in accordance with law. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal, J:- In this Rule Nisi the respondent Nos.1 and 2 have been called upon to show cause as to why the order of dismissal of the petitioner dated 20 January, 2003 purported to have been issued by the respondent No.1, Prime Bank Ltd. under the signature of respondent No.2 vide Memo No.H0/(HRD)/l 447/2003 dated 20th January, 2003 dismissing the petitioner from service of the respondent No.1 Prime Bank Ltd. with effect from 30.05.2002 should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are as under: The petitioner filed the writ petition on the averments that he jointed in service as principal officer of the respondent No. 1, Prime Bank Ltd. in 1995 and thereafter he got promotion from time to time for his sincere and honest work. The petitioner due to some obvious reason tendered his resignation on 20.05.2002 from the service of respondent No.1, Prime Bank Ltd. and also handed over his complete charge on 30.05.2002 without any objection whatsoever and thereafter, he joined in service as vice president of Premier Bank, Head Office on 01.06.2002 and on 02.05.2002 he was transferred to the Motijheel Branch as Manager and thereafter on 05.10.2002 he was transferred to the Premier Bank Ltd. Dhanmondi Branch as Manager. The respondent No.1 is a Banking Company incorporated under the Banking Companies Act, 1991, the respondent No.2 is the Managing Director of the respondent No.1, the respondent No.3 is the Central Bank of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (Bangladesh Bank) and respondent No.4 is the Premier Bank Ltd. being incorporated under the Banking Companies Act, 1991. However, after joining in the service of Premier Bank, the respondent -Prime Bank Ltd. started a departmental proceeding against the
petitioner for various irregularities and on that, the respondent Prime Bank Ltd. sent a show cause notice to the petitioner vide Memo No.H0/(HRD)/2654/2002 dated 14.09.2002 (Annexure-F to the writ petition) along with charge sheet vide Memo No. HO/ (HRD)/2655/2002 dated 14.09,2002 (Annexure-Ft). In response, to show cause notice the petitioner sent a reply to the respondent No. 1, Bank stating, inter-alia, that the petitioner was no longer in the service of Respondent No.1, who tendered his resignation on 20-05-2002 from the service of respondent-Bank and also handed over his complete charge on 30-05-2002 without any objection and as such after tendering his resignation and handing over the charge on 30.05.2002 the petitioner is no more under the service Rule of Prime Bank Limited, the allegations as embodied in the show cause notice and charge sheet are frivolous, mechanical, false and without any legal basis. Thereafter, the respondent-Prime Bank Ltd. under the signature of respondent No. 2(Managing Director, Prime Bank Ltd.) passed the impugned order dated-20.1.2003 dismissing the petitioner from the service of respondent No.1, Prime Bank Ltd. with effect from 30.05.2002. 

3. Feeling aggrieved with the order of dismissal dated 20.1.2003 passed by respondent No. 2(Managing Director, Prime Bank Ltd.) the petitioner approached this Court in an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and obtained the present rule. 

4. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 Prime Bank Ltd. contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-, opposition denying the allegations made in the writ petition contending that the grounds as set up in the writ petition are all untrue and baseless. The impugned order of 
dismissal singed by the Managing Director, Prime Bank Ltd. (respondent No. 2) who is not a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority and thus, the writ petition is misconceived one and therefore, it is not maintainable. 

5. Mr. Shamsuddin Babul, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in the course of his argument has taken us through the writ petition and other materials on record and then submits that the petitioner was no longer in the service of Respondent-Bank, who tendered his resignation on 20-05-2002 and, also handed over his complete charge on 30-052002 without any objection whatsoever and as such after tendering his resignation as well as handing over the charge on 30-05-2002 the petitioner is no more under the service Rule of Prime Bank Limited. He next, argues that the internal inquiry Committee of the Prime Bank Ltd. shows that there is no overt act against the petitioner for his personal gain rather the petitioner and others have acted only for the interest of respondent Bank as per the direction given by the Head Office but inspite, of that the issuance of impugned order of dismissal is nothing but issued the same with a malafide intention to create cloud over the future service of the petitioner in the financial institution. He further argues that during the tenure of the service of the petitioner in the Respondent Bank, the petitioner has not committed any irregularities or any supervisory lapses in discharging his official duty; that since May, 2000 he was never in charge of the foreign Desk rather he was the Deputy Manager only, he was in-charge of the Foreign Exchange Department until May, 2000 and for the said period. Bangladesh Bank Audit as well as internal Bank Audit also completed without any objection whatsoever; that from July, 2000 to June, 2001 the petitioner was neither dealing Officer in any desk of the foreign Exchange Department of Motijheel Branch and as such the allegations as brought in the charge-sheet against the petitioner are malafide, ill-motive and without any basis and as such the order of dismissal (Annexure-J) should be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Mr. Shamsuddin Babul, the learned Advocate for the petitioner to fortify his submission relied on the decisions reported in 55 DLR- 130, 33 DLR-430 and 5 PLD(1964)-647. 

6. On the other hand. Mr. A. S. M. Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 (Prime Bank Ltd.) after placing the affidavit-in-opposition straightforward submits that the impugned order of dismissal passed by the Managing Director, Prime Bank Ltd. (respondent No.2) who is not a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority and as such the instant writ petition is not maintainable. The learned Advocate in support of his sole contention heavily relied on the decisions reported in 4 MLR(AD)-347, 44 DLR-239 and 48 DLR.-431. 

7. These are the points which were argued by the learned Advocates of the respective parties. Admittedly, in this writ petition the petitioner challenged the order of dismissal passed by the respondent-No. 2, Managing Director, Prime Bank Ltd. is not a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority. Apart from the merits of the case, the main contention between the parties related to the maintainability of the application under Article 102 of the Constitution. 

8. To appreciate the points raised before us by the respective parties, we are first to see whether the writ petition is maintainable or not. In deciding the question of maintainability of this writ petition, we feel It necessary to reproduce the provisions as laid down in Article I 02(2)(a) of the Constitution, which deals with the requirement of filing the writ petition by the aggrieved person/s before this Court. 
Article 102(2)(a) of the Constitution reads as follows: 
(2) The High Court Division may, if satisfied that no other equally efficacious remedy is provided by law. 
(a) on the application of any person aggrieved, make an order-
(i) directing a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority to refrain from doing that which he is not permitted by law to do or to do that which he is required by law to do; or 
(ii) declaring that any act done or proceeding taken by a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority has been done or taken without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; or. 

9. A reading of these Articles together and as a whole, indicates that the High Court Division on the application of any aggrieved person, make an order directing a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority to refrain from doing that which he is not permitted by law to do or to do that which he is required by law to do or declaring that any act done or proceeding taken by a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority has been done or taken without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

10. It appears that in the instant writ petition the petitioner has impugned the order of dismissal (Annexure-J) passed by the respondent-No. 2, Managing Director, Prime Bank Ltd. who is not a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority. 

11. In the case of Manjurul Huq Vs. Bangladesh, reported in 44 DLR-239 wherein this Court observed as follows: 
"The impugned order Annexure-D dated 24.01.1991 (the contents of which have already been quoted above) has been passed by respondent No.3 Chief Adviser and Director General, Bangladesh Diabetic Association. The second impugned letter (Annexure-E) dated 28.01.1991 (contents of which have also already been reproduced above) is written by Prof. Wahiduddin Ahmed, Moha Sachib, Bangladesh Diabetic Association (presumably respondent No.4 or 5) who is also an officer of the Bangladesh Diabetic Association. Therefore, the orders or actions of the aforesaid employees of the Bangladesh Diabetic Association cannot be called in question by the petitioner before this Court under Article 102(2) (a) of the Constitution." 

In the case of Abdur Rahman Vs. Bangladesh reported in 48 DLR-43I this Court decided as follows: 
"Under Article 102 of the Constitution writ lies only against a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or local authority. Respondent No.3, Mobarakgonj Sugar Mills Limited is not a local authority though respondent No. 2, Bangladesh Sugar and Food Industries Corporation is a local authority. The order of termination was passed by the respondent No.3 and not, by the respondent NO.2. Though respondent No.3 is under the control of respondent No.2 the impugned order cannot be treated as an order passed by the respondent No.2. In the above facts and circumstances  and position of law we are of the view that the writ petition at the instance of the petitioner who was an employee of the respondent No.3, though not a worker, is not maintainable as no writ lies against the officer of a Company as he was not performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or a local authority." In the case of Abdur Rahman (MD.) Vs. National Tea Company Ltd. reported in 4 MLR (AD) -347, it has been held as follows: 
"Among others the High Court Division found that the writ petition was not maintainable because the National Tea Company has not been, established or created by the Government under any Act or Statute and as such it was not a local authority within the meaning of section 3(28) of the General Clauses Act read with article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution The petition is dismissed. 

12. In view of the provisions of Article IO2(2)(a) of the Constitution vis-a-vis the uniform decisions of the Highest Court as cited -above, we are constrained to hold that this application under Ankle 102 of the Constitution is not maintainable inasmuch as admittedly the impugned order of dismissal (Annexure-J) passed by the respondent-No. Managing Director, Prime Bank Ltd. is not a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority. By now we have got a clear view of the law as it stands today that under Article 102 of the Constitution writ lies only against a person performing functions connection with the affairs of the Republic or local authority. 

13. Mr. Shamsuddin Babel, the learned Advocate for the petitioner on the point of maintainability of the writ petition relying on the decision reported in 55 DLR-130 submits that Prime Bank Ltd. is a private Bank, though, in performing the functions the respondent-Bank acted under the Rules of Central Bank of Bangladesh (Bangladesh Bank) and therefore, it can not be said that no writ petition lies against the order or action of a private-Bank. 

14. We have carefully gone through the said decision to the best of our ability and find one Zakir Hossain Munshi as a subscriber of Graameen Phone being aggrieved for imposing royalty and licence fees every year preferred writ petition. In the case of Zakir Hossain Munshi Vs Bangladesh reported in 55 DLR-130, whereircfre Rule was made absolute on the ground that:- 
"In performing the above functions Grameen Phone has thus acted in the affairs of the Government and, as such, Grameen Phone is required to ensure accountability, transparency and bonafide in performing such functions. The service agreement entered into by and between the subscribers including the petitioner and Grameen Phone in this case is not an ordinary trading agreement but a contract entered in this regard for providing mobile telephone services by Grameen Phone as an agent and licensee of the Government. Therefore, any act of Grameen Phone in breach of the contract or showing lack or want of transparency and bonafide on its part as complained of by the petitioner is accountable in writ jurisdiction of this Court." 

15. In the instant case we have already noted that the petitioner was an employee of respondent-Prime Bank Ltd. challenged the order of dismissal ( Annexure-1) passed by the respondent-No. 2, Managing Director, Prime Bank Ltd. who is not a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority. Therefore, the decision reported in 55 DLR- I 30 has no manner of application in the facts and circumstance of the case as the facts of instant case are quite distinguishable from the facts of that case. On consideration of the matter we find no force or substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

16. Since the petitioner has failed to across the first hurdle as to the question of maintainability, we need not embark upon detail discussion as to the legality or otherwise of the impugned order.

17. In view of the above, we do not therefore find any merit in this Rule. 

18. Accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs. 


End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Syed Md. Ziaul Karim .J:- Plaintiff petitioner on presentation of a petition under Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure(briefly as Code) seeks Review of a judgment dated 28-02-2007, recorded by this Court in Civil Revision no.5049 of 2004, discharging the Rule arising out of the judgment and order dated 09-11-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Pabna. in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 18 of 2004, affirming those of dated 25-04-2004 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Pabna, in Other Class Suit No. 72 of 2003; rejecting an application for temporary injunction. 

2. The only question, that survives for determination in this Review petition is whether the Judgment recorded by this Court, discharging Rule, can be at all
reviewed keeping in view the laws and principles regulating Review enshrined in Order XLVII Rule I of the Code and temporary injunction postulated in Order XXXIX Rules I and 2 of the Code.  

3. For the purpose of answering to the question posed facts relevant may succinctly be stated and noticed. 

4. On 27-10-2003 the petitioner as plaintiff instituted. Other Class Suit No. 72 of 2003, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Pabna, impleading the opposite parties as defendants for declaration that the letter dated 18-10-2003 issued under the signature of Chairman of the Governing body of Md. Yeasin Degree College (Opposite party No.1) suspending the petitioner from the post of Assistant Professor Psychology Department is illegal, without jurisdiction, void and not binding upon the petitioner. On, the some date the plaintiff also filed an application under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of the Code for temporary injunction for restraining the defendants. 
(a) from approving the order of suspension dated 18-10-2002, 
(b) from dismissing her from the service, 
(c) and from stopping the Government allowance. 

5. Eventually, after hearing the trial Court by ifs order dated 25-04-2004 rejected the said application for temporary injunction, however directed the defendants to pay 50% Government allowances. On appeal, the same was affirmed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Pabna. Both the Courts below concurrently held that the application for temporary injunction is pre-mature. 

6. Plaintiff petitioner felt dissatisfied of the above adjudication of the matter and invoked this Court's Revisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of The Code on presentation of Revision Petition and obtained Rule. Revision Petition had been numbered as Civil Revision no. 5049 of 2004. After hearing, this Court by the judgment and order dated 28-02-2007 discharged the Rule on the following grounds: - 
"On consideration of the materials on record, I find that the order of suspension was for temporary period and the final order was not passed. Therefore 1 hold that the application for temporary injunction was pre-mature. Both the Courts below concurrently held that the plaintiff has no prima facie case and the application for temporary injunction was pre-mature. I do not find any reason to differ with such concurrent views." 
AND
"In the instant case, the plaintiff failed to show any one of the aforesaid principles: Moreover, the trial Court directed to the concerned authority of the College to. pay 50% of the Government allowance to the plaintiff. It further appeais that the Courts below concurrently held that the plaintiff will not suffer any irreparable loss or injury by the impugned decision of the College. Moreover, no final order has Yet been passed against the plaintiff I am also in agreement with the aforesaid concurrent views of the Courts below." 

The petitioner could not be satisfied with the decisions recorded by this Court and sought review of decisions on carrying this review petition before this Court. 

7. Mr. Abdul Matin Khashru, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr. Pankaj Kumar Kundu, Advocate, for the petitioner seeks to impeach the impugned judgment dated 28-02-2007 passed by this Court on the three folds arguments. Firstly, the subject-matter of the impugned shoW cause notice and the impugned order of suspension are different. Both the Courts below failed to consider the same and committed error of law. Secondly, the petitioner earlier filed a criminal case against some members of the governing body of the College and on such grudge they issued the impugned order of suspension with malafide intention. Thirdly, the resolution dated 24-03-2002 shows the name of the Chairman but his signature was not available in the resolution. So, according to him the entire proceedings adopted against the petitioner with malafide intention. In support of his contention, the learned Counsel refers the case of Altaf Hossain (Md) Vs. Md. Abdul Rahim and others reported in 51 DLR-527, wherein it is held;-  
"When a person is suspended without any material whatsoever against him and he had been kept in that conditions for months together the Court should interfere in such a case in the interest of justice." 
8. The learned Counsel also refers the case of Bijoy Kumar Shaha Vs. DC, Chuadanga and others, reported in 55 DLR-550 wherein it is held: "Suspension of an employee pending a disciplinary proceeding is an approved measure and the Court does not generally interfere with it. But if the order of suspension is prima facie illegal and tinged with malafide, the Court is competent to act for preventing  injustice.

9. The learned Counsel lastly submits that in view of the aforesaid facts the petitioner established a prima-facie case for obtaining an order of temporary injunction and as such the judgment and order dated 28-02-2007 passed by this Court may be reviewed. 

10. Mr. Md. Nazrul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos. 12, 4,6-10 opposes the review application and submits that the questions of malafideness are the disputed question of facts which can not be decided by this court without taking evidence. He adds that there is no mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or any other sufficient reason to review the judgment passed by this Court on 28-02-2007. Therefore, the application for review is liable to be rejected. 

11. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Counsels, I have gone through the impugned judgment dated 28-02-2007 along with other materials on record and given my anxious consideration to their submissions. 

12. In backdrop of factual matrix of matter and also, wake of grounds pressed into service, question posed may now be approached and answered. 

13. In approaching and answering the question posed, it will be profitable to notice scope of Review first. Review Jurisdiction visualised by section 114 of The Code is to be traced to Order XLVII, rule 1 of The Code which contains prescribed condition and limitation in terms of requirement of that section. Order XLVII, rule 1 of The Code before Civil Procedure Code (Amendment) Ordinance of 1962 runs thus: 
1.(1) Any person considering himself aggrieved

 (a) by a decree or order from which an appeal is allowed, but from which no appeal has been preferred,
 (b) by a decree or order from which no appeal is allowed, or 
(c) by a decision on a reference from Court of Small Causes,
 and who, from the discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge or "could not be produced by him at the time when the decree was passed or order made-"„ or on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or for any other sufficient reason, desires to obtain a review of the decree passed or order made against him, may apply for a review of judgment to the Court which passed the decree or made the order. 

14. The word "or could not be produced by him", or the words, " for any other sufficient reason" stood omitted by Civil Procedure Code (Amendment) Ordinance of 1962 (Ordinance No. XLIV of 1962) which came into force on June 5, 1962. 
Review now can be sought and made only on two specific grounds which are: 
i. From the discovery of new and. important matter or evidence which after exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge when the decree was passed or order made. 
ii. On account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record. 

15. The Court of Review, thus, got only a limited jurisdiction circumscribed by definitive limits fixed by language employed in Order XLVII, rule I of The Code. 

16. Review is not a rehearing of a case. Review is not an appeal, or, to put it differently, Review is by no means an appeal in disguise whereby an erroneous decision stands corrected. Not mere error of fact and law, but error apparent on the face of the record is a ground for Review. Review lies only on a patent error. There is real distinction between a mere erroneous decision and an error apparent on the face of the record. Error apparent on the face of record is an error which can be seen by mere perusal of record without reference to any other matter and to find out such error one has not to scrutinise the evidence or record but it should be self-evident from a perusal of the record itself and can be pinpointed without elaborate examination. 

17. In the case of Basharatulah being dead his heirs. Fazle Karim and others Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 16 BLD(AD) 9=48DLR(AD)178 wherein it has been observed that: 
Order XLVII Rule of the code of Civil Procedure contemplates Review of the judgment or an order under specified conditions-
(I) On, the disco very of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge  
(II) On account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or 
(III) for any other sufficient reason. 
unless a prayer for review is based on the grounds mentioned, the court will not sit on the matter again for a re-hearing or further hearing which. is already concluded by decision.

18. This view receives support in. the- cases of Govt. of West Pakistan Vs- Gulzar Mohammad reported in 21 DLR (SC) 46. Buxly paints (BD)Ltd Vs- Bangladesh reported in 31 DLR (AD)-266, Asaduzzaman -Vs- Bangladesh reported in 36 DLR(AD)-1 08, Halima Zaman and others Vs- Govt of Bangladesh and others 18 BLD-296, Md. Amin khan. Vs- controller of Estate duty PLDI962 (SC)-335. Nurul Hosein Vs- Govt. of Bangladesh 4 9 DLR(ADII OS. Serojuddin. Ahmed and others. Vs- Govt. or Bangladesh 14 BLT (AD)I47. Azizulla @ Azizur Rahman Vs- Abu Taher Chowdhury and others II MLR (AD)-129, A Mannan Akand Vs- Md. Lutfor Rahmann and others 14 BLT(AD)-211, Siddique (Md) Master Vs- Shamsul Hurt and others 8 BLC-688. 

19. Now, the principles relating to granting temporary injunction may be looked into. 

20. In the case of Mst. Aymun Nessa and others Vs. Md. Obaidul Haque and others reported in 35 DLR 25 wherein the principles for granting injunction has been enunciated in the following manner: 
"Three well-established principles of km governing the grant of temporary injunction are the following: First, the plaintiff' has to establish a prima facie case. Secondly, it was to he shown that the plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss if the injunction prayed for is not granted and thirdly, the balance of convenience lies in favour of the plaintiff and in favour of granting the temporary injunction prayed for.

 In the instant case, the plaintiff failed to show any one of the aforesaid principles and as such she is not entitled to get an order of temporary injunction. 

21. I have carefully considered the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioner. The submissions made and the grounds taken, in the review petition may hold good in the trial Court at the time hearing of case. At this stage, there is no scope to go into those matter. Therefore, his contentions are repelled. 

22. In view of the discussions made above and the preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities referred to above, I am of the view that the Review petition has got no merit and as such the same, thus, stands rejected in limini. 

End.
